    Share transfer of a consolidated subsidiary
    The Company resolved at a meeting of the Board of Directors held on April 24, 2025 to sell all of its shares of
    Ajinomoto Althea, Inc. (“Althea”), a sterile fill-finish CDMO and a 100% subsidiary of the Company, to
    Packaging Coordinators Inc. (“PCI”), and signed a share transfer agreement with PCI on the same day.
    (1) Reason for share transfer
          Althea provides aseptic fill-finish services for clinical- and commercial-stage biopharmaceutical
          customers as a member of Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services. PCI is a leading global contract development
          and manufacturing organization (CDMO) providing clients with integrated end-to-end drug development,
          manufacturing, clinical trial services, advanced drug delivery services and commercial packaging
          technology services, which has been actively investing to expand its fill-finish capacity and capabilities,
          as exemplified by the acquisition of Lyophilization Services of New England, Inc. in 2021. Although this
          transaction impacts on financial results of the Company in the fiscal year ended March 2025, we have
          concluded that, given Althea and PCI’s strengths and service offering, PCI is the best partner for Althea
          to continue its growth and maximize its value to customers.
          In accordance with the Medium-term ASV Management 2030 Roadmap announced in February 2023,
          the Group is pursuing growth by focusing on the four focused growth areas where high market growth
          potential as well as high social value are expected, leveraging the strengths of “AminoScience.” Within
          the Healthcare area, we are focusing on high value-added services driven by our proprietary technologies.
          As part of this strategy, we acquired Forge Biologics Holdings in November 2023, entering into a gene
          therapy CDMO business.
          The Group continues to operate CDMO business with focus on further developing high value-added
          services where it can leverage its proprietary technologies and aims to accelerate growth and realize
          strong profitability in the Healthcare area.
    (2) Overview of Althea
          (i)     Company name:                      Ajinomoto Althea, Inc.
          (ii) Number of shares outstanding: 100 shares
          (iii) Description of business:             Drug product fill-finish and formulation services
    (3) Overview of transfer of Althea shares
          (i)     Share transfer date:               May 1, 2025
          (ii) Number of shares transferred: 100 shares
          (iii) Transfer costs:                      US$27 million (after price adjustment)

6. Research and development activities
   In the years leading up to 2030, we aim to become a company that contributes to the well-being of all human
   beings, our society and our planet with “AminoScience.” “AminoScience” is a collective term for the various
   materials, functions, technologies, and services derived from research and implementation processes
   rigorously focused on the functions of amino acids, since our founding. It also refers to the Ajinomoto Group’s
   unique scientific approach to connect these to resolving social issues and contributing to well-being. This is
   one of our sources of the Group’s competitive advantage, which cannot be easily imitated by other companies.
   Toward 2030, we will realize the outcomes of “Reducing our environment impact by 50%” and “Helping
   extend the healthy life expectancy of 1 billion people” by contributing to the environment in conjunction with
   solutions to health and nutritional issues. In terms of the Ajinomoto Group growth strategies, we leverage
   “AminoScience,” the unique strength of the Ajinomoto Group, in markets with potential for medium- and
   long-term growth. Focusing on four growth areas (Healthcare, Food & Wellness, ICT, and Green) in which we
   can provide sustainable social value, we will achieve dramatic growth in the years leading to 2030 by steadily
   expanding our existing businesses and using business model transformation (BMX) to drive growth.


   During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, research and development expenses for the Ajinomoto Group
   amounted to ¥32,108 million.
   The Ajinomoto Group holds approximately 4,280 patents in Japan and overseas.
   Below is an overview of our R&D activities in each business segment and their results during the fiscal year
   under review.
   (1) Seasonings and Foods segment
        Our R&D efforts are led by the Institute of Food Sciences and Technologies of the Company, which
        works closely with the research and development divisions of Group companies in Japan and overseas,
        including Ajinomoto AGF, Inc., Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc., and SHANGHAI AJINOMOTO
        FOOD RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CENTER CO., LTD. (China). Our technical development,
        product development, and application development cover every element that makes up deliciousness,
        such as taste, aroma/flavor, and texture.
        Japan has been at the forefront of developing solutions to issues such as falling birthrates, aging society,
        shrinking household size, and health consciousness. The Ajinomoto Group has been refining models to
        address these issues in Japan without compromising “Taste,” “Access (Delivering nutrition to
        everyone),” and “the Local Way of Life,” and now is extending them worldwide. Led by our global
        product development system, we use our marketing and brand strengths to continuously develop sauces,
        seasonings, and processed food products that fit the tastes and needs of consumers in individual
        countries.

        Sauce & Seasonings (Japan)
        In the Japanese market, we are elevating our seasoning design technology and psychological value design
        technology to provide both home cooking convenience and authentic delicious flavor. In products such as
        the “Cook Do®” series, we use our proprietary AJI-EMap® psychological value design technology to
        visualize the sense of satisfaction and elation that consumers seek from food, and reflect our findings in
        flavor, aroma, richness, and aftertaste design. Also, based on our Deliciousness Technology, we design
        the formulation of oil, fat and spice, and design the aroma of products taking into consideration how their
        aromas change with heat. Through this, we create products with stable quality even when there are
        variations in the cooking process. Furthermore, we combine our powdering technologies, blending
        technologies, and dissolving control technologies to make our products easier to work with when cooking
        and better able to achieve reproducible results.
        In FY2025, we released new products that applied these technologies, focusing on our Chinese and
        Korean sauces and seasonings and the general purpose sauce and seasoning field. In the “Cook Do®
        Today’s large plate” series, we released <Sesame Tantan-style Pork and Japanese Radish Stir-fry>,
        which combines the flavor of sesame and the aroma of spice with the richness of broth and fermented
        seasonings. This product is designed to enable consumers to cook a satisfying main dish just by stir-
        frying meat and vegetables in a frying pan. In the “Cook Do® KOREA!” series, we released <Bibimbap
        Stir-fry>, which is based on authentic Korean gochujang and beef broth, with the optimal blend of
        fragrant garlic and sesame oil. The quality design of this product lets people create authentic Korean
        dishes in their own homes.

                                                       - 59 -
In the “Steam Me®” series of products designed with an eye towards the cooking process with heating
elements, we have released <Moist Steamed Chicken Breast>. With our unique ingredient formulation
and pressure steam pouch, we enable foods to retain moisture even when they are cooked in a
microwave, achieving technologies that ensure that chicken breast, which tends to dry easily, stays moist.
In the main dish and Western sauce and seasonings field, we launched <Aromatic Bolognese> from
“Pasta Cube,” which can be cooked with a single frying pan. It perfectly combines the richness of beef
and the flavors of fragrant vegetables and herbs to create a taste that is hard to reproduce at home.
From the perspective of ingredient selection, we released <Cage-free Egg Mayonnaise>, a product made
with eggs from cage-free chickens raised in Yamanashi Prefecture using natural circulation farming
methods, whose quality design leveraged the richness and smoothness of its raw materials.
Through these initiatives, the Group is working to simplify cooking and improve quality reproducibility.
At the same time, we’re also deepening the value of sauces and seasonings rooted in Japanese cuisine and
responding to the diversifying consumer tastes and cooking situations.

Sauce & Seasonings (overseas)
In overseas markets, we are developing products based on the food cultures, consumer preferences,
health issues, and social issues in different countries and regions. Ajinomoto Vietnam Co., Ltd. has
developed “Aji-mayo®,” which has all of the delicious taste of mayonnaise but with 30% less fat. This is
an example of social implementation of our research and development results to address nutritional issues
while keeping taste satisfaction. PT Ajinomoto Indonesia has used our design and production know-how
for seasoning pastes developed in Japan to develop seasoning products for quickly making stews, helping
shorten the amount of time consumers spend on housework.
We will continue to pursue deliciousness backed by the Group’s unique ingredients and technologies
while reinforcing our product development to offer greater health value and cooking convenience,
providing delicious flavors tailored to local preferences and contributing to health and lifestyles.

Quick Nourishment (Japan)
In FY2025, in the Quick Nourishment segment, we continued to develop products that are delicious and
have nutritional value, given increasingly sophisticated consumer needs for instant foods and easy-to-
prepare foods.
In our soups and noodle (pasta) processed food products, we have designed products to offer highly
satisfying flavors and textures in home cooking through the use of technologies for heating and
powdering fragrant vegetables and by researching how to improve restoration using hot water. We have
applied these technologies to our “Knorr® Cup Soup” potage series and to “Soup DELI®” soup pasta
products characterized with its chewy yet soft pasta.
In FY2025, we launched the <Ripe Tomato Pasta> and <Three Cheese Carbonara> varieties of “Soup
DELI® PASTA+,” which contains even more pasta for a greater sense of satisfaction. Thanks to our
unique technologies for controlling restoration using hot water, these products have an excellent texture
despite being easy-cook products.
In our formulation design, we focused on the sense of consistency between soup, noodles, and toppings,
striving to achieve both an authentic feel and chewiness for <Tom Yum Kung Noodle> in our “Yum
Yum®” brand. Furthermore, we are improving our formulation design and our dissolvability technologies
to make it easy for customers to get nutrients they need, like protein and amino acids, through their
regular meals. Our “Ajinomoto KK Protein Miso Soup” is made using our unique Deliciousness
Technology. It has the bold, delicious flavor of miso soup, and our dissolvability technologies make it
easy to dissolve in hot water.
Furthermore, in the soup field, we launched “Knorr® SakuSaku de Copain,” which uses new techniques
to combine the texture of bread with the delicious taste of soup. The product aims to provide greater
culinary experience value in an instant soup form through its structural design, which keeps the bread
crispy even after pouring in hot water.
In the instant Japanese food field, we leveraged the fruits of our years of research into Japanese broth
“dashi” to launch “Dashiya Miso Soup.” The powder design leverages the features of dashi ingredients to
create instant miso soups that enable consumers to easily enjoy the flavor of dashi in their busy daily
lives.

                                              - 60 -
Through these initiatives, the Group is striving to provide cooking convenience, quality, and nutritional
value while creating Quick Nourishment value that matches consumers’ diverse dining situations.

Quick Nourishment (overseas)
In the overseas Quick Nourishment field, we are developing products that leverage the functions of
amino acids while respecting the different food cultures, consumer preferences, resources, raw materials,
and stakeholders of the countries and regions where we do business. Specifically, to address issues such
as reducing salt intake or increasing protein intake, we are providing products tailored to local markets,
using formulation designs and processing technologies to keep great taste while increasing nutritional
value. For example, Ajinomoto Co., (Thailand) Ltd. has developed a seasoning formulation for its
“YumYum®” instant noodles that uses our Deliciousness Technology to supplement the decrease in
saltiness and the decline in richness and flavor that came from reducing salt content. In the future, we
will pursue deliciousness backed by the Group’s unique ingredients and technologies, and continue to
intensify our research and development activities in the health value field to contribute to great taste that
matches the preferences of consumers in various regions while improving nutrition.

Coffee Products
In FY2025, in the Coffee Products field, we developed products with added health value and convenience
while keeping the great flavor of coffee, reflecting the diversification of consumer preferences and
drinking situations. We refined our coffee extraction design method, flavor design, and formulation
technologies to expand the value of beverages so that they can be seamlessly incorporated into our
customers’ day-to-day lives.
To meet the needs of health-conscious consumers, the Blendy® Mainichi no Chokatsu Coffee (Daily Gut
Healthy Coffee) series is designed to have the great taste of coffee while being easy to drink and
contributing to the health of customers’ intestinal environments. In FY2025, we introduced a 60 g bag
version and a 14 stick black coffee version to make it easier for customers to enjoy the product as part of
their daily routine. With these products, we are providing health value through the everyday drinking of
coffee.
We have updated our stick coffee products by using a new creaming powder to improve the flavor that
Blendy® Stick users place such great importance on, and we have made these products even more
delicious by achieving the optimal balance of tastes for each flavor in the series. With the aim of
broadening the range of consumer preferences supported, in the Blendy® CAFÉLATORY® Stick series,
we carried out product development focused on ingredient combinations and aroma. As one of the
products in the Hojun series, we developed Hojun Grapefruit Jasmine Tea (Rich Aroma Grapefruit
Jasmine Tea), which combines grapefruit and jasmine tea, with a formulation that aims for the perfect
balance of tea beverage flavor and fruit flavor. This meets the needs of consumers who place great
importance on both sweetness and fragrance.
Also, in the Blendy® Portion series, to meet the growing demand for ice-based drinks and customized
recipes in the home, we are developing products by formulating blends using fruit, tea leaves, and matcha
ingredients. In FY2025, we launched the new Fruit Tea Three Fruit Mixes and Matcha au Lait Base and
also improved the flavor of Black Tea. Furthermore, for Blendy® My Bottle Stick, focusing on a form
that is easy to carry and convenient to consume, we developed three products in the iikoto mainichi series
(Something Good Every Day series). These are the first products with functional claims for the brand.
They are designed to enable consumers to develop a healthy habit by simply dissolving a stick in their
own water bottle, and they support drinking situations while on the go or while at work.
Through these research and development efforts, the Ajinomoto Group is promoting product designs for
the coffee and beverage field that offer great taste and health value while meeting the needs of
increasingly diverse drinking scenarios.

Solution & Ingredients
In FY2025, we focused on the clean label market, which is expanding primarily in North America and
Europe and for which there are many requests from customers. Through our development of unique
ingredients made using fermentation technology, such as fermented tomato and Kokumi substances
which produce richer flavor, and the application of these ingredients in our production, we are working to



                                               - 61 -
    increase the value of deliciousness we provide in both the consumer product field and the restaurant and
    industrial-use product field.
    For our fermented tomato ingredients, we have developed techniques for producing and enhancing the
    spiced feel and the fresh tomato feel of the ingredients. We have begun using these ingredients in both
    consumer products and restaurant and industrial-use products. For consumer products, we are
    supplementing the initial fresh tomato flavor and depth of products which use tomatoes, such as Knorr®
    Cup Soup Potage Made with One Whole Ripe Tomato, helping produce a satisfying flavor even after
    cooking, despite the soaring price of ingredients. We have also launched “AROMAX🄬🄬 Punch Up” which
    contain fermented tomato, for processed foods, supplying them to food processors as raw materials to
    give foods a greater sense of spice flavoring and freshness.
    In our yeast extract ingredients, we have turned our attention to functions for increasing the richness of
    initial flavors and developed technologies for giving finished products a greater feel of ripeness and
    richness, as well as contributing to a greater feel of saltiness. We have rolled out these ingredients in our
    consumer products such as our series of flavor seasonings. These fermentation technologies are
    undergoing functional verification in North America and around the world, and they are being used as
    unique ingredients that improve both initial flavor and flavor depth in various fields.


    Research and development expenses for the Seasonings and Foods segment amounted to ¥8,388 million.

(2) Frozen Foods segment
    At the Research and Development Center of the Ajinomoto Frozen Foods Co., Inc. and the development
    divisions of Group companies overseas, we are developing products that match local tastes and needs.
    Furthermore, through collaboration with the Institute of Food Sciences and Technologies of the
    Company, they are working to provide greater health value, such as salt reduction.

    Frozen Foods (Japan)
    In the frozen foods category, in FY2025, we developed products for a wide range of dining situations,
    from everyday home meals to individual portions and healthy meals, in response to increasingly diverse
    consumer lifestyles and the need to shorten cooking times. In addition to expanding our lineup, primarily
    focusing on meal-at-home categories, we also strove to enhance the value provided by frozen foods
    through product designs that offered cooking convenience, quality stability, and nutritional value.
    In our frozen “AJINOMOTO BRAND GYOZA,” we have continued to use Ajinomoto Frozen Foods
    Co., Inc.’s raw material formulations, pan-cooking condition design, oil and fat design, and other unique
    technologies to develop gyoza that do not stick to the pan when cooked and have more consistent
    finished quality. We have improved the formulation of our base for the hane (crispy layer) and optimized
    the cooking conditions in a quality design that produces an excellent gyoza skin feel and juicy gyoza
    fillings whether they are cooked in a frying pan or a microwave. We also use a large volume pack and
    trayless packaging design to improve storability in homes and make the products easier to use.
    In our frozen chicken packaged food product field including karaage, we are developing technologies that
    make foods easy to prepare and also taste delicious. In addition to our flagship products made with
    chicken thigh meat, we are also developing products that make it easy to serve dishes that are hard to
    cook at home by optimizing spice usage, marinating conditions, and cooking processes. In FY2025, we
    rolled out our <Bite-sized Tandoori Chicken>, which has an authentic spicy fragrance and soft, juicy
    texture, and developed new <Protein Chicken Thigh Karaage> that blends chicken thigh meat with soy
    protein for high protein content along with excellent texture and flavor. These products are healthy and
    delicious owing to our unique formulation designs and seasoning/marinating technologies. Also, to meet
    demand for high levels of protein, we are developing frozen food products like <Protein Pork GYOZA>
    and <Protein Shumai> that allow customers to efficiently take in protein. These products are designed to
    offer greater nutritional value without negatively impacting the meaty texture or mouthfeel, so people can
    easily take in protein within their daily diets.
    In our “The★” brand of frozen foods for enjoying restaurant quality at home and our “YoshokuTei”
    Hamburg steaks, we strive to improve both fragrance and texture by reviewing and revising our
    ingredient formulation, cooking conditions, and sauce design. These products are improved to give
    greater satisfaction as main dishes, and have a quality design tailored to microwave oven use, which
    reduces the workload involved in cooking.
                                                   - 62 -
    The “Obento PON®” series of dishes for box lunches uses unique packaging and container designs, such
    as naturally thawing designs and stick packaging, to reduce the effort involved in cooking while also
    reducing waste. In addition, in our “Mirai CYCLE” series that uses irregular products from our
    manufacturing process, we sold <Fuzoroi Petit Canelé (petit canelé with cosmetic imperfections) > in a
    new initiative aimed at reducing food loss and waste while offering delicious taste.
    Furthermore, in the fields of frozen fried rice and rice bowl topping, we have developed formulation
    designs and production methods that produce authentic flavors and enable easy preparation.
    Through these research and development efforts, the Group is adapting frozen foods to diverse dining
    situations and enhancing the provision of products that are convenient, tasty, and nutritious.

    Frozen Foods (overseas)
    Due to Japanese food becoming well-established and Asian food demand increasing in North America
    and Europe, the Asian frozen food market has continued to grow, especially in the retail market. In North
    America, we have launched gyoza with hane (crispy layer), which were previously sold primarily in
    Asian markets and club stores, in general retail stores as well. We have expanded our merchandise lineup
    that showcases ease of cooking and great taste developed in Japan. In conjunction with this, we are also
    striving to increase awareness among a wider range of consumers through our expansion into retail
    channels and through our promotion activities.
    In Europe, we have expanded our lineup of products including gyoza and Japanese snacks, and enhanced
    our expansion in the retail market. In addition to making improvements to existing products, we are
    developing merchandise matched to local preferences and dining situations. As a result of these efforts,
    we are becoming better established among non-Asian consumers and expanding our sales areas.
    In the ASEAN and Central and South American markets, we have carried out initiatives aimed at a full-
    fledged entry into the frozen food market. We are verifying market features and operation suitability
    while also working on the creation of supply systems.
    In the future, we will use the production technologies and merchandise development capabilities we have
    nurtured in Japan to supply products that offer cooking convenience and great taste. We will also
    continue to develop frozen foods with health functions and added value. Through these initiatives, we
    will contribute to the sustained growth of our overseas frozen food business.

    Research and development expenses for the Frozen Foods segment amounted to ¥1,956 million.


(3) Healthcare and Others segment
    We work together with the Research Institute for Bioscience Products & Fine Chemicals, the Institute of
    Food Sciences and Technologies, Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma Services businesses (Belgium, US, Japan,
    India), ZAO “Ajinomoto-Genetika Research Institute” (Russia), Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Co., Inc., and
    other Group companies and their technical development divisions in Japan and overseas, to supply
    products and solutions that contribute to the health and lives of people across the world.

    Amino Acids for Pharmaceuticals and Foods
    To respond to the growth of the market for Amino Acids for Pharmaceuticals and Foods, we are
    continuing to develop and introduce fermentation and purification processes with the goals of increasing
    productivity and cost competitiveness. Also, in the culture media business for culturing animal cells, we
    are using Ajinomoto CELLiST Korea Co., Inc. as a platform to continue and expand development in
    conjunction with Japanese and global biopharmaceutical manufacturers.

    Bio-Pharma Services (CDMO Services)
    In the Bio-Pharma Services business, we globally operate pharmaceutical contract development and
    manufacturing organization (CDMO) business through our sites in Belgium, the United States, Japan,
    and India. We provide integrated services ranging from process development to GMP manufacturing for
    active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and intermediates used in small-, middle-, large-molecule, and
    gene therapy pharmaceuticals. We supply the innovative and unique AJIPHASE®, CORYNEX®, and
    AJICAP® platform technologies, as well as oligonucleotide synthesis, antibody drug conjugates (ADC),

                                                  - 63 -
highly active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing, continuous flow manufacturing, and other
services, covering everything from pre-clinical use to commercial production.
In the oligonucleotide field, we have created a development and manufacturing system that covers
everything from low-volume, high-mix production through solid-phase synthesis by GeneDesign, Inc. to
high-volume manufacturing using AJIPHASE® liquid-phase synthesis. We are promoting business by
strengthening our coordination with S.A. Ajinomoto OmniChem N.V. In the ADC field, our unique
AJICAP® site-specific antibody conjugation technology improves manufacturing efficiency and ensures
consistent quality. We are expanding our external partnerships through initiatives such as a license
agreement with Astellas Pharma Inc., and collaborations with NJ Bio, Inc. and Piramal Pharma Solutions,
while enhancing research and development support for customers. We are working to expand our
business and maximize our social contributions by strengthening our external partnerships, such as
establishing a sustainable manufacturing platform for peptides and proteins that are in high demand as a
result of partnering with Olon S.p.A. on our CORYNEX® microbial expression technology.
Forge Biologics, Inc., a US-based gene therapy CDMO that became a consolidated subsidiary in
FY2023, has strengths in adeno-associated virus (AAV) manufacturing and plasmid manufacturing,
which are key steps in the value chain. It provides high-purity, high-yield AAV vector manufacturing
services. Furthermore, we are reinforcing our technology base through joint development of culture
media and other products with the aim of improving our AAV productivity, striving to expand and enrich
our research and development systems and supply systems in the gene therapy CDMO business.

Functional Materials (Electronic Materials and Others)
In the electronic materials field, with Ajinomoto Fine-Techno Co., Inc., we develop “ABF™,” key
insulating material widely used in advanced semiconductor packages for servers, data centers, personal
computers and mobile applications. ABF™ offers excellent insulation reliability, processability, and fine-
line patterning capability, supporting the continued advancement of semiconductor packaging
technology.
Driven by the rapid growth of AI, cloud computing, and data-center infrastructure, semiconductor
packages are increasingly required to deliver higher bandwidth, lower power consumption, and greater
integration density. To address these needs, the Group is researching and developing materials for Co-
packaged optics, which integrate optical and electrical interconnects within a single package. In addition
to conventional insulating materials for semiconductor packages, we are developing polymer optical
waveguide materials and related integration technologies that enable optical interconnections with a
focus on achieving low dielectric constant and low dielectric loss tangent characteristics, thereby
contributing to the realization of next-generation photonic-electronic packages.
Through these research and development efforts, we aim to contribute not only to conventional
semiconductor packages, but also to next-generation semiconductor packages, as well as advanced
communications infrastructure.

Others
—Functional nutritional foods—
aminoVITAL® is a functional nutritional food brand launched in 1995 that applies the findings of
“AminoScience,” which we have been developing for over a century, to the sports field. For many years,
it has earned the trust of top athletes and individuals engaged in intensive physical training. At the same
time, we have worked at international sporting events and competitive sports sites to verify our
knowledge of amino acid replenishment and refine our product designs. These initiatives provide an
important foundation of feedback for our research and development based on real-world usage
environments.
In recent years, as participation in sports has broadened and health consciousness has increased, we have
expanded our research and development focus beyond sports into everyday life, with the aim of
contributing to the physical and mental well-being of a wider range of consumers who incorporate
exercise into their daily routines. In FY2025, the 30th anniversary of the brand, we developed
“aminoVITAL® amiKatsu,” a jelly drink that can be easily enjoyed in day-to-day life, such as a part of
additional breakfast item or as a snack.
It contains amino acids (3,000 mg) such as alanine, proline, BCAA, and arginine which can serve as
energy substrates, while also providing nutrients that are often insufficient in the diet, such as vitamins

                                               - 64 -
and dietary fiber. In developing the product, we utilized the Ajinomoto Group’s proprietary target quality
design technology, AJI-PMap®, to identify sensory attributes suited to morning consumption, when jelly
drinks are most commonly consumed. As a result, the product delivers a distinctive texture and flavor
that provide the sensation of eating real fruit.
We also launched aminoVITAL® CONNECT Joint Support, a product designed with a focus on
maintaining physical function. Drawing on the fact that collagen is rich in specific amino acids, the
product contains 4,000 mg of six amino acids—serine, sodium aspartate, glutamic acid, glycine, alanine,
and proline—which have been reported to help alleviate knee joint discomfort in individuals
experiencing discomfort in their knee joints.
Through these research and development initiatives, the Group has built upon the scientific knowledge
accumulated through supporting top athletes and is creating new value in the field of functional
nutritional foods with a broader focus on exercise habits and health maintenance in daily life. In doing so,
we continue to expand the real-world application of “AminoScience.”

—Fundamental foods—
In the field of fundamental foods, we are developing products based on research into the physiological
functions of amino acids and other functional ingredients, with the aims of supporting the establishment
of healthy habits that can be maintained easily in everyday life. In FY2025, we reinforced our lineup of
food with functional claims, with a focus on energy metabolism.
“Capsi EX®” contains dihydrocapsiate, a functional ingredient found in abundance in non-pungent chili
peppers. The product supports increased energy expenditure at rest, which is a part of daily energy
metabolism. While the product had previously been marketed primarily through direct-to-consumer
channels, in FY2025 we launched the new <60 Capsule Pouch (General retail version)> for sale in retail
stores, expanding the available product formats and making it easier for more consumers to incorporate
the product into their daily routines.
This product was designed to meet the needs of consumers who seek to manage their health as part of
their day-to-day lives, without engaging in intensive exercise or special activities. It represents one
example of the “fundamental foods.” The Group will continue to develop products that support health
maintenance and improvement by combining scientifically validated functional ingredients with formats
that encourage regular, long-term use.

—Personal care ingredients—
In 1972, the Ajinomoto Group released Amisoft®, an amino acid-based surfactant made with glutamic
acid. Ever since then, for over half a century, we have been supplying ingredients in amino acid-derived
cosmetics and toiletry products to over 5,000 cosmetics manufacturers and other companies in 55
countries. The Group’s personal care ingredients based on “AminoScience” are not just easy on the skin
and hair, but are also exceptional at moisturization, feel great, and are environmentally friendly. They are
used in a wide range of fields, including skin care, hair care, makeup, and other products.
We developed “AMIHOPE® SB-201,” an amino acid-derived functional powder for use in skincare and
makeup products, and launched it in FY2025. This product uses unique surface design technologies
based on its amino acid-derived ingredients to prevent powder clumping, producing a smooth feel and a
uniform spread. Furthermore, it offers a better usage feel and finish than conventional powders and it is
environmentally friendly. Because of this, we have high hopes for its use in diverse cosmetic
formulations.
Leveraging our strengths as an ingredient manufacturer, we are also expanding our JINO brand of
skincare products specializing in cosmetic ingredients made with our own amino acids. We are carrying
out research and development integrated with our materials research and product development. In
FY2025, we updated “JINO” <Amino Ceutical Cream> and began selling it exclusively through e-
commerce sites. In designing this product, we had turned our attention to the functions of amino acids
within the body, and we created a formulation of 23 amino acids, with various functions, to address all
kinds of skin issues. The new updated version of the product uses our unique Amino Beauty Theory®,
which is based on long years of skin science research by the Research Institute for Bioscience Products &
Fine Chemicals of the Company. We enhanced the product’s approach to improving the state of skin
cells.


                                               - 65 -
    We also reflected the fruits of our research on skin condition fluctuations and barrier functions in our
    “JINO” brand products. In February 2026, we began selling “JINO” <Amino Barrier Oil>, which
    contains a high concentration of “ELDEW®” amino acid-based emollient oil, exclusively through e-
    commerce sites. This product was designed to retain moisture and protect skin from irritation through the
    power of the amino acid-derived ingredient. This ingredient is also widely used as a cosmetic ingredient
    in skincare and makeup products to keep lips and skin moisturized.
    Furthermore, we turned our attention to the protein structure of the skin and established a unique skincare
    concept of an approach to four proteins that make up beautiful skin, from the stratum corneum to the
    dermis. These research results have been reflected in our products, such as in our updated “JINO”
    <Amino Ceutical Cream>, with multi-level moisturizing and skin firming care designs based on
    balancing amino acid composition. Through these research and development efforts, the Group is
    creating value for personal care ingredients that contribute to healthy skin and the well-being of
    consumers by combining material technologies and product development based on “AminoScience.”

    Research and development expenses for the Healthcare and Others segment amounted to ¥11,292
    million.

(5) Corporate
    By backcasting from our future vision in the years from 2030 to 2050, we aim for business expansion in
    the fields which show promise for the future of the Ajinomoto Group, and carry out corporate research of
    related research topics, focus our resource investment, and engage in development work. In our corporate
    research, the Institute of Food Sciences and Technologies and the Research Institute for Bioscience
    Products & Fine Chemicals of the Company play a central role, coordinating with other research
    organizations in Japan and overseas to leverage pioneering research and technologies, developing new
    technologies and unique materials and ingredients for various businesses together with other research
    labs within the Group, and reinforcing fundamental technologies shared by different businesses.
    We are also increasing our investment in intangible assets. Firstly, our technology assets include
    “AminoScience,” represented by our Deliciousness Technology and cutting-edge bioscience and fine
    chemical technology. Going forward, we believe that digital capabilities will be vital to better meeting
    the needs and wants of our customers. We will increase our investment in human assets that match our
    customers and technologies to generate innovation, as well as in customer assets and organization assets
    that serve as the foundation of these assets.

    Open innovation
    We actively promote open innovation, and we believe that it is an important management theme to create
    new and unprecedented value by partnering with companies, research organizations, and other
    organizations in Japan and overseas. To help globally accelerate our innovation in growth areas of the
    Ajinomoto Group, our Innovation Strategy Teams coordinate with various internal organizations
    (corporate venture capital, research and development divisions, business divisions, etc.) and external
    partners across the globe to formulate and execute organic and inorganic growth strategies.
    These teams are based in Japan, North America, Europe, Latin America, and ASEAN. In North America,
    to strengthen our framework for partnering with startups and to accelerate the sourcing of advanced
    innovation intelligence, we have a new corporate venture capital (CVC) office in Silicon Valley (Palo
    Alto, California). Furthermore, to globally accelerate our innovation in growth areas such as healthcare,
    we also have an office in the Boston area, which is the hub of the innovation ecosystem, and are sourcing
    advanced technologies and promoting collaborations with outside partners.
    In addition, in Europe and the ASEAN region, we are also partnering with diverse innovators, such as
    universities, research institutes, and startups, exploring technologies based on the features of each region,
    and creating collaboration opportunities. These global hubs serve as the foundation that supports the
    global activities of our Innovation Strategy Teams. These teams are tasked with our intelligence functions
    (Search, Access & Partnering) to directly access leading global innovation trends, enabling the swift


                                                   - 66 -
evaluation and decision-making for investments, partnerships, and M&As toward creating next-
generation businesses.

Our main open innovation activities in FY2025 were as follows:
—Healthcare area—
By using pioneering bio-technologies based on “AminoScience,” the Group is shifting its healthcare
business into the high-added-value healthcare business. In FY2023, we made Forge Biologics, Inc. a US-
based gene therapy CDMO, a fully consolidated subsidiary. Through our full-fledged entry into the next-
generation medicine field, which includes gene therapy, we are accelerating our growth in the Healthcare
area and increasing our profitability.
In our partnership with Forge Biologics, Inc., we have developed supplements for cellular culture media
that improve the efficiency of virus vector production, an elemental technology in gene therapy drug
development. We use our expertise in amino acids and culture media design, developed over the course
of many years, to improve the efficiency of virus vector production processes and achieve more
consistent quality.
Furthermore, in the biopharmaceutical field, we are developing technologies that support the manufacture
of next-generation pharmaceuticals, including antibody drug conjugates (ADCs). In FY2025, we
concluded a technology license agreement with Astellas Pharma Inc. for the development and
manufacture of ADC active pharmaceutical ingredients. Through this, we are externally rolling out
development and manufacturing technologies for our biopharmaceuticals while also striving to strengthen
our technical foundation in the pioneering medicine field.
Furthermore, in the medical nutrition field, we completed our investment in Enhanced Medical Nutrition
Inc. (Ontario), a Canadian surgical nutrition startup. This investment has enabled us to coordinate US-
based Ajinomoto Cambrooke, Inc. and the existing medical food business of Nualtra Limited, which has
sites in the UK and Ireland, to further strengthen our development of solutions for addressing the
nutritional problems faced by patients, including perioperative patients.


—Food & Wellness area—
To achieve well-being through food, we are creating new value in the Food & Wellness area by using
digital technologies and collaborating with outside partners. In FY2025, we worked to create an
integrated system for supporting nutritional design, menu creation, and operation efficiency improvement
for restaurant and industrial markets, which includes catering and employee cafeterias.
Specifically, we collaborated with Chi-technology Co., Ltd., which develops systems and software
packages for the catering industry. Through this collaboration, we combined our own knowledge
regarding nutritional design with the company’s operation systems and began verification testing aimed
at providing menus optimized for diverse customer needs, such as delicious flavor, nutrition, and price. In
this verification, we are using AI to create menus and provide nutritional management support, and
verifying that both well-balanced diet and a reduction in the workloads of those in the field can be
achieved.
We have also begun application service provider business aimed at refining dietary and nutritional
management in medical facilities and companies. In this business, we are using our nutrition design
technologies and data to provide highly specialized nutritional management and menu support as digital
services, promoting the health of users and helping improve operational efficiency.
Furthermore, to improve the eating environments of working people, we have begun collaborating with
OKAN Inc., which provides the Okigata Shashoku® service. This collaboration improves access to
nutritionally balanced meals in diverse working environments, like offices and factories, and helps
promote greater health consciousness and behavioral changes among employees.
We will continue to combine our nutrition design technologies and products based on “AminoScience”
with the digital technologies and services of outside partners to tackle the food-related issues faced by
individuals and organizations, accelerating the establishment of well-being in the Food & Wellness area
throughout society.




                                              - 67 -
—ICT area—
Sales of ABFTM, a vital insulating material for high-performance semiconductors, are continuing to grow,
driven by the evolution of semiconductor packages. The sources of that competitiveness are our unique
material technologies, which are based on “AminoScience,” and our close co-creation ecosystem with
key players in the semiconductor industry value chain. We have created a system that enables us to
anticipate the properties needed for next-generation semiconductor packages through our collaborations
with customers and related companies and to rapidly reflect them in material designs.
Furthermore, another strength of the Group is our High-speed Development System, which leverages our
knowledge regarding polymer chemistry, our molecular design capabilities, and our formulation
technologies. We use this system to continuously refine ABFTM. The evolution of ABFTM is supporting
improvements in wiring miniaturization, communication speeds, energy savings, and other
semiconductor package advances, which contributes to the development of society’s ICT infrastructure,
such as AI, data centers, and autonomous driving.
As data communication volumes grow, power consumption levels rise. To deal with this problem, we are
leveraging the material technologies and co-creation framework that we nurtured through ABFTM with
the aim of supplying solutions that reduce power consumption and improve performance for next-
generation semiconductor packages that fuse optical and electrical technologies.
In addition, while ABFTM business is our core business in this area, we are also extending technologies to
peripheral areas. By developing magnetic materials, encapsulants, ABF-RCC (resin-coated copper foil),
and others, we are expanding the value we provide in the semiconductor materials field. We are also
working with outside partners to carry out exploratory activities in new ICT fields such as bioelectronics,
looking to 2030 and beyond.
In this way, the Group’s open innovation in the ICT field is not stopping with the development of
standalone technologies, but consists of a co-creation ecosystem and high-speed development. We will
continue to anticipate the needs of society and users, refining our technologies and contributing to the
realization of a smart society as an innovation provider that is vital to the semiconductor industry.


—Green area—
We are using the Group’s “AminoScience” strengths to aim for a positive impact of reducing GHG
emissions by 1.6 million tons per year by 2030. We will accomplish this by building sustainable food
systems and conducting agro-solution business. In the Green area, we are working to supply sustainable
foods that contribute to environmental sustainability and the well-being of consumers through our Green
Food business, agro-solution business, and livestock feed business.
Last year, we began the development and verification of a developed nation business model in Singapore,
and we are now selling “Atlr.72®” brand sweets. This fiscal year, we are expanding into the staple food
category and implementing a high-speed development model that agilely verifies direct store sales and
makes improvements, and then offers processed food products with ongoing demand potential through
general retail channels.
To expand next-generation sustainable foods, we have invested in Australia-based v2food Pty Ltd, which
is creating a version 2 of meat, a next-generation sustainable food, made from plant protein. This has
provided us with the company’s expertise and technologies related to vegetable protein. We combine
those expertise and technologies with our Deliciousness Technology and our global business platform to
accelerate our development of ingredients and foods with smaller environmental impacts and their use
throughout society.
In the agro-solution business, we are helping make farming more efficient, improve crop quality, and
reduce environmental impacts, primarily through our biostimulant business. We decided to become a
participating partner in the “Demonstration Survey for Restoration of Degraded Agricultural Land in
Brazil” project, one of the initiatives of the Japan-Brazil Green Partnership Initiative (Japan-Brazil GPI)
being conducted under the Japanese and Brazilian governments. We will supply biostimulant products
such as AJIFOL® liquid leaf surface spray and AMINO Arginine to a model farm in Brazil and verify
their effectiveness. By effectively using byproducts and circulating resources back to farming land to
establish a biocycle, we will contribute to the development of sustainable agrifood systems.
Furthermore, in response to calls by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development
Organization (NEDO) for proposals for its Research and Development of Technologies to Promote

                                               - 68 -
Biomanufacturing project, we proposed “the development of precision fermentation technologies that
would help protect the environment while stabilizing the food supply,” and this proposal was selected for
implementation. This research utilizes our knowledge and unique pioneering bio-technologies in the field
of fermentation production, which we have developed through the years, along with AI and simulations,
to improve and accelerate production process development for efficiently and steadily performing
commercial production of target proteins. Through this, we aim to strengthen our technology base with
an eye towards social implementation.

Corporate research and development expenses amounted to ¥10,382 million.

(8) Share ownership plan for directors (and other officers) and employees
     The Company has introduced a Medium-term Stock-based Incentives (MTI) plan (the “Plan”), with the
     aim of achieving sustained medium- to long-term improvement in business performance and increasing
     corporate value of the Ajinomoto Group. Under the Plan, the Company contributes up to ¥2.2 billion to a
     stock-granting trust (the “Trust”), and the Trust acquires the Company’s shares. After the end of the
     three-year trust period, performance is assessed using a predetermined evaluation indicator, and the Trust
     pays the Company’s shares and the amount equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the Company’s
     shares (the “Company’s Shares, etc.”) to the eligible persons. They must be Executive Officers (including
     those who concurrently serving as Directors) of the Company during the target period. The maximum
     number of the Company’s shares to be granted to the Eligible Executive Officers is 1.1 million.
     The number of the Company’s shares to be granted to the Executive Officers is calculated by multiplying
     the evaluation indicators calculated based on the target achievement rate and the assessment weighting
     for each evaluation indicator, by the amount of the pre-set medium-term performance-linked
     remuneration by officers’ ranks and then dividing the product by the closing price of the Company’s
     shares on March 31, 2023 (¥2,303.0). (Shares less than 100 are rounded down.) Half of the compensation
     will be delivered in the form of Company shares, and the remaining 50% will be used for payment of
     income tax, etc., therefore the Trust will convert this to cash by selling the shares on the market and then
     paying the amount equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares. The Medium-term
     Stock-based Incentives (MTI) is paid to non-residents of Japan in the form of cash compensation.
     Those who newly become Executive Officers during the target period will be paid the Company’s
     Shares, etc., calculated on a monthly pro-rata basis according to the duration of their term of office as an
     Executive Officer. In the event of a change in position due to promotion, etc., during the target period,
     the Company’s Shares, etc. will be paid by proportionally calculating the Company’s medium-term
     earnings performance evaluation index in accordance with the duration of the term of office in the
     position before and after the change. If an Executive Officer retires along the way (excluding
     resignations for personal reasons contrary to the Company’s wishes), they will receive Company Shares,
     etc. on a monthly pro-rata basis according to the length of their tenure. However, in the event of death or
     becoming a non-resident of Japan, a cash amount equivalent to the disposal value of the number of the
     Company’s shares calculated on a monthly pro-rata basis according to the length of their tenure will be
     paid.
     The evaluation indicators, target values, and assessment weighing for the Medium-term Stock-based
     Incentives (MTI) covering the three fiscal years beginning in FY2023, as resolved by the Compensation

    less than one unit from June 1, 2026 to the filing date of this Annual Securities Report. It also does not deduct shares sold in
    response to requests for the sale of shares less than one unit.




                                                                 - 82 -
3. Dividend policy
   The Company’s basic policy is to pay dividends twice a year, an interim dividend and a year-end dividend,
   with the interim dividend determined by the Board of Directors and the year-end dividend determined by the
   General Meeting of Shareholders. The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that, except as otherwise provided for
   by laws and regulations, dividends from surplus and other matters set forth in respective items of Article 459,
   Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act may be determined by a resolution of the Board of Directors. While the
   Articles of Incorporation stipulate the payment of year-end dividends as described above, in principle, the
   payment of such dividends is determined by a resolution at a General Meeting of Shareholders, except in cases
   where infectious diseases or natural disasters may affect the holding and operation of the General Meeting of
   Shareholders.
   In the Medium-term ASV Management 2030 Roadmap, the Company has declared a progressive dividend
   policy, indicating a policy of increasing or maintaining dividends without reducing them, and plans to pay an
   annual dividend of ¥48 (interim dividend ¥24) per share for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, an increase
   of ¥8 from the previous fiscal year. The Company’s standard dividend calculation method is based on
   normalized EPS (Note), which uses business profit less affected by extraordinary profit fluctuations such as
   from impairment losses.
   The Company will continue to work to further increase dividends by steadily increasing business profit, and
   the total return ratio (to profit attributable to owners of the parent company) for the three-year period is set at
   50% or more.
   Based on these factors, the Company plans to increase an annual dividend by ¥2 from the current fiscal year to
   ¥50 per share (with an interim dividend of ¥25 per share) for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.
   Internal reserves will be allocated first to support organic growth, with M&A as the next priority to drive
   further business expansion. In addition, the Company will conduct flexible share repurchases within a net
   interest-bearing debt/EBITDA ratio of less than 2.0x.
   Note: Dividends based on normalized EPS = (Business profit × (1 − Ajinomoto Group standard tax rate at 27%)) / Total number
         of shares outstanding × Return coefficient at 35%

4. Status of corporate governance, etc.
   (1) Overview of corporate governance
         (i)   Basic approach to corporate governance
               The Ajinomoto Group positions corporate governance as one of the most important aspects of its
               management foundation for strengthening the ASV Management and achieving our “Vision for
               2030.” Toward 2030, we accelerate the ASV Management for achieving “the extension of healthy
               life expectancy of one billion people” and “the reducing of our environmental impact by 50%”
               through initiatives of both resolving health and nutritional issues linked by food systems and
               promoting sustainability. Furthermore, in order to enhance the effectiveness of ASV Management,
               we select a “Company with Three Committees” that clearly separate supervision and execution by
               balancing “supervision of appropriate execution that reflects the opinions of stakeholders” and
               “business execution with a sense of speed.” In order to ensure the sustainable enhancement of
               corporate value over the medium to long term, the Board of Directors, which consists of a variety of
               Directors, indicates a major direction by discussing and examining important management matters
               that greatly affect our corporate value, supports risk-taking in execution, and appropriately
               supervises execution by verifying the validity of execution processes and results. On the other hand,
               the execution, the Chief Executive Officer who has been greatly delegated authority from the Board
               of Directors will take the lead in making decisions for important business execution at the Executive
               Committee, will realize sustainable enhancement of corporate value as One Team. In order to
               closely communicate between the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee, governance
               rules are established based on the Company’s approach to enhance corporate value, proposals and
               reports are made from the Executive Committee to the Board of Directors, and deliberations and
               resolutions are made by the Board of Directors.
               Recently, in the changes in the external environment, comprehensive risk management is important
               than ever. We honestly comply with the Ajinomoto Group Policies (hereinafter, “AGP”)
               (https://www.ajinomoto.com/sustainability/agp/) that shows the ideal way of thinking and action
               that Ajinomoto Group companies and their officers and employees should comply with, continue to
               develop and properly operate our internal control system, strengthen our system that considers
               sustainability as an active risk-taking system, and continuously enhance our corporate value.


               The Principle on Corporate Governance of Ajinomoto Co., Inc. is available on the following
               website.
               https://www.ajinomoto.co.jp/company/en/ir/strategy/corp_gov.html

New Seven Important Management Matters
In conjunction with the transition to a Company with Three Committees in FY2021, the Company has set
out the “Seven Important Management Matters” that we believe will have a significant impact on
corporate value in the medium to long term, and we have been discussing them at the Board of Directors
meetings. In the evaluation of the effectiveness of the Board of Directors in FY2023, there were opinions
that in order to realize Our Vision for 2030, set out in the Medium-term ASV initiatives 2030 Roadmap,
the matters to be discussed by the Board should be reconsidered. There was also a proposal that in order to
realize Our Vision for 2030, it is necessary to set an even longer-term vision for the Company than 2030,
while understanding changes in the business environment over the longer term. Based on these findings, in
FY2024, after multiple discussions with the Board of Directors, the Company reviewed the “Seven
Important Management Matters.” In setting the “New Seven Important Management Matters,” we
established three frameworks: (i) define Ajinomoto Group’s long-term Vision, (ii) discuss how the
Ajinomoto Group should move forward to achieve medium- to long-term growth and create future value,
and (iii) strengthen the foundation of corporate activities that will serve as the basis for the challenges in
realizing growth and creating value. Based on these frameworks, the Board of Directors has identified the
important management matters that should be discussed by the Board of Directors in order to sustainably
enhance corporate value.

- Nomination Committee
  The Nomination Committee deliberates on validity of the evaluation and reappointment of Directors, on
  validity of the evaluation and reappointment of Representative Executive Officer & President, and on
  succession planning of the Representative Executive Officer & President, etc. The Nomination Committee
  decides the policy of electing and dismissing Directors, proposals for the election and dismissal of
  Directors, and proposals of draft for selection of the Representative Executive Officer & President, etc.
  The Nomination Committee consists of three or more members, with a majority of Independent Outside
  Directors. Members of the Nomination Committee are selected from among the Directors by resolution of
  the Board of Directors.
  The Nomination Committee shall, in principle, include three or more Independent Outside Directors, and
  the Chair of the Nomination Committee shall also be selected by resolution of the Board of Directors from

                                                        - 87 -
  among the Independent Outside Directors who are Members of the Nomination Committee. The
  Nomination Committee’s resolutions or deliberations are appropriately reported to the Board of Directors
  by the Member of Nomination Committee selected by the Nomination Committee.

- Audit Committee
  The Audit Committee plays an important role in the function of “supervision of business execution” by the
  Board of Directors by auditing the legality and appropriateness of Executive Officers and Directors’
  business execution.
  The Audit Committee consists of three or more members, with a majority of Independent Outside
  Directors. Members of the Audit Committee are selected from among the Directors by resolution of the
  Board of Directors.
  The Audit Committee shall, in principle, include three or more Independent Outside Directors, and at least
  one Director with substantial knowledge of finance and accounting. The Chair of the Audit Committee
  shall also be selected by resolution of the Board of Directors from among the Independent Outside
  Directors who are Members of the Audit Committee. The Audit Committee’s resolutions or deliberations
  are appropriately reported to the Board of Directors by the Members of Audit Committee selected by the
  Audit Committee.

- Sustainability Advisory Council
  To enhance corporate value from a sustainability perspective, the Sustainability Advisory Council has
  been established as a subordinate body of the Board of Directors, with the objective of making
  recommendations on the Company’s approach to sustainability. In the second phase of the Sustainability
  Advisory Council, which commenced in April 2023, the Council evaluated the initiatives for execution
  regarding the matters referred to the Board of Directors: “Implementation of materiality (Implementation),
  information disclosure and dialogue regarding implementation (Communication), and building
  relationships with stakeholders (Partnership).” It submitted a final report to the Board of Directors in
  March 2025. The final report highlighted expectations for strengthening “building relationships with
  stakeholders” in order to deliver greater value beyond the scope of a single company. In response, for
  FY2025, the Council set two themes: “sustainability-related rulemaking” and “sustainable finance,”
  including consideration of collaboration with international organizations and financial institutions. It also
  held two rounds of discussions between Directors and external experts, with the outcomes of these
  discussions shared with the Executive side.


- Outside Directors Communication Committee
  The Company established the Outside Director Communication Committee with the aim of enhancing
  the effectiveness of the Board of Directors through the exchange of information among the Independent
  Outside Directors and through the mutual complementation of specializations.

                                                                                                                        May 14, 2026
                                                                                               Board of Directors, Ajinomoto Co., Inc.

                                 Result of the 11th Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Board of Directors

1. The Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Board of Directors in Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
   The Ajinomoto Group has grown through initiatives to co-create social and economic value through its businesses. We refer to
   these initiatives as ASV (Ajinomoto Group Creating Shared Value), which serves as our fundamental management policy
   (“ASV Management”).
   The Board of Directors, through the ASV Management, works with stakeholders and others to resolve social issues, contributes
   to the realization of a sustainable society, and takes responsibility for sustainable enhancement of corporate value. In order to
   fulfill this responsibility, we have defined the “effectiveness” of our Board of Directors as follows and have been undertaking
   various initiatives aimed at establishing a highly effective Board.

     The “Effectiveness” of our Board of Directors:
        How appropriately the Board of Directors fulfills its objective of properly indicating major directions by
        discussing and examining important management matters that greatly affect our corporate value, supporting risk-
        taking in execution, and appropriately supervising execution by verifying the validity of execution processes and
        results.
                       * Three core elements of “Effectiveness” of our Board of Directors




   In fiscal 2025, marking the 11th evaluation, we conducted the evaluation as outlined on the section below titled “2. Details of
   Evaluation Process in FY2025.” In this evaluation, in order to clarify the evaluation criteria, we defined the roles of the Chair
   of the Board and the Chairs of the three statutory committees, as well as the “effectiveness” of the three statutory committees,
   and conducted the evaluation based on these definitions (the details of which are described later). In addition, while the
   Company has conducted effectiveness evaluations of the three statutory committees in conjunction with the Evaluation of
   Board Effectiveness, in this evaluation, we are disclosing, for the first time, the results of the effectiveness evaluations of these
   committees. For details, please refer to “4. Results of the Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Committees.”

3. Results of Evaluation of Board Effectiveness
   (1) General Overview
       We evaluated that our Board of Directors appropriately demonstrates its “Effectiveness” as defined by us. We will continue
       to pursue initiatives aimed at further enhancing this effectiveness going forward.

    (2) Improvements based on the Results of the Previous Evaluation
        The Board of Directors conducted a comprehensive review of the “Seven Important Management Matters” that it should
        deliberate on in fiscal 2024, as outlined below.
                     Framework                              New Seven Important Management Matters
             Defining our vision           · Analysis of Future External Environment and Long-term Vision
                                           · Portfolio and Resource Allocation, and Intangible assets
             Achieving medium- to          · Financial and Capital Policy
             long-term growth and          · Sustainability
             creating future value         · Organizational Execution Capabilities (Speed up & Scale up)
                                           · Stakeholder Engagement
             Strengthening the
