                                               * Please refer to the “Principle on Corporate Governance of Ajinomoto
                                                   Co., Inc.”

        Based on the above, in the previous evaluation of Board effectiveness (fiscal 2024), the Board of Directors, through
        discussions, confirmed its approach to “To indicate major directions,” in order to effectively advance deliberations based on
        the “New Seven Important Management Matters” commencing in fiscal 2025.

        In fiscal 2025, the Board proceeded with deliberations based on the “New Seven Important Management Matters.”
        (a) In particular, significant progress was made in “Governance.” While the strengthening of group governance is one of the
             Company’s key themes, a shared recognition was reached with the executive side that the development of the group
             compliance framework should be prioritized. Through detailed discussions on the executive side and multiple rounds of
             deliberations at the Board of Directors, this led to the establishment of the “Group Compliance Committee,” a
             subordinate body of the Executive Committee, effective April 1, 2026. This is considered to be an example in which
             close discussions between the Board and the executive side have enabled the strengthening of the foundations of
             corporate activities. The Board will continue to further consider other themes beyond the group compliance framework.
        (b) In addition to the above, with respect to areas such as “Analysis of Future External Environment and Long-term Vision,”
             “Portfolio and Resource Allocation, and Intangible assets,” and “Financial and Capital Policy,” the Board evaluates that
             a certain level of progress has been achieved through deliberations at the Board of Directors.

    (3) Overview of Board Discussions and Responses to Identified Issues
        Based on the results of the survey and interviews, the Board held deliberations to further enhance its effectiveness. The main
        points of these deliberations are outlined below.

        Discussion on “Indicating Major Directions,” One of the Three Core Elements of Effectiveness
        In the survey and interviews, taking into account the progress of various deliberations based on the “New Seven Important
        Management Matters” in fiscal 2025, some Directors expressed the view that there remains a need to further deepen the
        understanding of how the Board of Directors should “indicate major directions” this year as well. Based on these views, the
        Board deliberated on “To indicate major directions.”
        With regard to “To indicate major directions,” the Board confirmed its recognition that the value lies not in the Board
        independently formulating proposals, but in a process of expanding and deepening discussions through dialogue between the
        Board and the executive side based on proposals presented by the executive side, thereby enhancing the quality of
        considerations on the executive side. In this process, the Board also shared the recognition that it is important for the Board
        to present issues, risks, and options from diverse perspectives, thereby conducting discussions that enable the Company to
        maximize its strengths.
        As the Board of Directors, based on these discussions, we will continue to conduct substantive deliberations, including those
        on the “New Seven Important Management Matters,” and strive to further enhance the effectiveness of the Board.

4. Results of Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Committees
   In conjunction with this Evaluation of Effectiveness of Board of Directors, evaluations of effectiveness were also conducted for
   each statutory committee. In conducting these evaluations, each committee defined the effectiveness of the committee and the
   role of its chair, and conducted the evaluation based on these definitions. The results of these evaluations were reported to the
   Board of Directors by the respective Chars of committee as outlined below.

                                                               - 94 -
                                             Results of Evaluation of Effectiveness
Nomination   The Nomination Committee evaluated that it appropriately demonstrates the effectiveness it aims
Committee    to achieve.
             In order to further enhance the effectiveness evaluation, the committee defined the effectiveness of
             the committee and the role of its Chair. In addition, in the deliberations on CEO succession
             planning and the nomination of director candidates, the committee ensured fairness, transparency,
             and objectivity through various initiatives, including conducting interviews with candidates on
             multiple occasions, reflecting insights obtained through concurrent service on other committees,
             and engaging in communication with stakeholders. Through these efforts, the committee
             contributed to the enhancement of corporate governance and the sustainable enhancement of
             corporate value.
             On the other hand, it was confirmed that there remains room to further strengthen the effectiveness
             of the Nomination Committee by advancing efforts to identify internal and external talent pools in
             order to ensure appropriate selection of future director candidates. While maintaining the
             independence of the Nomination Committee, which is composed entirely of Independent Directors,
             the committee will consider enhancing communication with Internal Directors in order to support
             discussions regarding the composition of the Board of Directors.

             [Definition of the Effectiveness of the Nomination Committee]
             To contribute to the enhancement of corporate governance and the sustainable enhancement of
             corporate value by ensuring fairness, transparency, and objectivity in the deliberation and
             resolution of the appointment and dismissal of Directors and the Representative Executive Officer
             & President (including evaluation and appropriateness of reappointment), as well as succession
             planning.

             [Definition of the Role of the Chair of the Nomination Committee]
             The Chair of the Nomination Committee shall have the primary roles: to play a central role in
             appropriately planning and operating the committee, including setting agendas and managing
             proceedings, in order to ensure that active discussions are conducted regarding the appointment
             and dismissal of Directors and the Representative Executive Officer & President, with fairness,
             transparency, and objectivity; and to engage in communication with stakeholders, including
             through IR activities, as necessary.
Audit        The Audit Committee evaluated that it appropriately demonstrates the effectiveness it aims to
Committee    achieve.
             Based on surveys of both Internal and Independent Directors, the committee determined that its
             effectiveness is being adequately fulfilled, as its recommendations are reflected in the execution of
             operations by the executive side through activities such as on-site audits of domestic and overseas
             entities, responses to the Audit Committee hotline, regular exchanges of opinions with the
             Representative Executive Officer & President and others based on these activities, submission of
             written opinions to the President on individual matters and follow-up thereof, and regular reporting
             to the Board of Directors.
             While there are no urgent issues requiring improvement, the committee will continue its activities
             with a focus on the following points:
             · To conduct agile Audit Committee activities in response to rapidly changing external
                environments.
             · To further improve efficiency in data analysis and report preparation through the use of
                generative AI.

             [Definition of the Effectiveness of the Audit Committee]
             To fulfill the effectiveness of the Audit Committee by reporting the results of various audit
             activities to the Board of Directors in a timely manner, based on the fundamental policy of auditing
             the execution of duties of Directors and Executive Officers as a representative of stakeholders,
             promoting lawful and socially reliable business execution within the Group, preventing misconduct
             and recurrence, and contributing to sound corporate governance and the enhancement of corporate
             value.

             [Definition of the Role of the Chair of the Audit Committee]
             The Chair of the Audit Committee shall have the primary roles: to play a central role in
             appropriately planning and operating the committee, including setting issues and managing
             proceedings, in order to maximize the committee’s ability to audit the execution of duties by
             Directors and Executive Officers (including responses to the Audit Committee hotline) and to
             perform duties such as decisions on the appointment and dismissal of accounting auditors, while
             effectively drawing on the capabilities of its diverse members; and to engage in communication
             with stakeholders, including through IR activities, as necessary.




                                                  - 95 -
Compensation     The Compensation Committee evaluated that it appropriately demonstrates the effectiveness it
Committee        aims to achieve.
                 In order to enhance the effectiveness evaluation, the committee defined the effectiveness of the
                 committee and the role of its Chair. The committee sought to improve objectivity and fairness by
                 deepening discussions using external market information regarding executive compensation, with
                 the aim of establishing compensation that contributes to the medium- to long-term enhancement of
                 corporate value. In this process, interviews were conducted with Executive Officers who also serve
                 as Directors to deepen understanding of expectations for and issues with the compensation system.
                 In addition, through communication with stakeholders, necessary information was obtained and
                 disclosed, contributing to enhanced transparency. From an organizational perspective, the
                 committee ensured independence by being composed solely of Independent Directors, while also
                 utilizing information obtained through members’ concurrent service on other committees to support
                 comprehensive deliberation and decision-making.
                 As areas for improvement, the committee identified the need to substantively verify the
                 contribution of the compensation system to corporate value enhancement and to evolve the manner
                 of reporting to the Board of Directors. The committee will continue to consider these matters from
                 a medium- to long-term perspective, including evaluation methodologies.

                 [Definition of the Effectiveness of the Compensation Committee]
                 To contribute to the enhancement of corporate governance and the sustainable enhancement of
                 corporate value by appropriately fulfilling the purposes of (i) compensation that contributes to the
                 medium- to long-term expansion of corporate value, (ii) maintaining a sufficiently competitive
                 level, and (iii) making decisions through a transparent process, through the execution of duties
                 related to the compensation of Directors and Executive Officers.

                 [Definition of the Role of the Chair of the Compensation Committee]
                 The Chair of the Compensation Committee shall have the primary roles: to play a central role in
                 appropriately planning and operating the committee, including setting issues and managing
                 proceedings, in order to ensure active discussions based on fairness, transparency, and objectivity
                 so that the committee can maximize its effectiveness; and to engage in communication with
                 stakeholders, including through IR activities, as necessary.




  < Business Execution/Executive Committee >
  The Chief Executive Officer who has been greatly delegated authority from the Board of Directors will
  take the lead in making decisions for important business execution at the Executive Committee, will
  realize sustainable enhancement of corporate value as One Team.
  The Executive Committee will realize prompt and appropriate business execution with a team centered on
  the Chief Executive Officer based on the major directions and mandates indicated by the Board of
  Directors. Deliberations and resolutions on basic plans, policies, and other important matters related to
  business execution will be described in the minutes along with the approval and disapproval of the
  members of the Executive Committee. In addition, proposals and reports to the Board of Directors are
  conducted in accordance with the Regulations on Board of Directors and the Minor Regulations on Board
  of Directors, and close communication is made so that the agenda of the Board of Directors can be set
  systematically and effectively.
  Members of the Executive Committee are consisted of the Representative Executive Officer & President
  and the other Executive Officers appointed by the Representative Executive Officer & President.


< Internal control, risk management and sustainability >
- Group Compliance Committee
  The Company has established the Group Compliance Committee (“GCC”) as a subordinate body of the
  Executive Committee for the purpose of preventing any loss of corporate value resulting from misconduct
  and contributing to the strengthening of the management foundation and the sustainable enhancement of
  the corporate value of the Ajinomoto Group.
  The GCC shall be primarily responsible for developing the global compliance framework and strategies of
  the Ajinomoto Group, providing overall management of AGP, and the operating the “Ajinomoto Group
  Hotline,” and responding serious compliance incidents.


                                                      - 96 -
  The GCC, on the occasion of each quarterly meeting, compiles and reports to the Executive Committee
  and the Board of Directors the contents deliberated and the status of activities of the GCC.

- Sustainability Committee
  In order to promote sustainability management, the Company has established the Sustainability
  Committee as a subordinate body of the Executive Committee.
  The Sustainability Committee works with the Risk Management Committee to select and identify risks
  and opportunities based on important issues (Materiality), as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto
  Group, making proposals to the Executive Committee. The Sustainability Committee then formulates
  countermeasures against risks and opportunities relevant to sustainability and manages their progress. In
  addition, the Sustainability Committee formulates the entire Ajinomoto Group’s sustainability strategy,
  promotes action themes (nutrition, environment, and society) based on this strategy, makes proposals and
  provides support for business plans from a sustainability viewpoint, and compiles internal information on
  ESG.

- Risk Management Committee
  The Company has established the Risk Management Committee as a subordinate body of the Executive
  Committee in order to identify risks, which interfere the achievement of the Medium -Term ASV
  Management Roadmap, as well as in order to establish and implement measures for risk management. The
  Risk Management Committee works with the Sustainability Committee to select and identify risks and
  opportunities based on important issues (Materiality) as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto
  Group, making proposals to the Executive Committee. Additionally, the Committee formulates various
  measures for risk management, particularly for risks that management should take the initiative to address
  (such as geographical risks and information security risks), and formulates risk management measures and
  manages their progress in order to realize a strong corporate structure capable of responding promptly and
  appropriately to risks and crises.

- Investment, Loan and Business Scrutiny Committee
  The Investment, Loan, and Business Scrutiny Committee carries out multifaceted reviews of investment
  and loan decisions, prior to deliberations by the Executive Committee.

- M&A Committee
  The M&A Committee carries out multifaceted reviews of M&A deals prior to deliberations by the
  Executive Committee.

         2)    Reasons for adoption of current corporate governance system
               The Ajinomoto Group positions corporate governance as one of the most important aspects of its
               management foundation for strengthening the ASV Management and achieving our “Vision for
               2030.” Toward 2030, we accelerate the ASV Management for achieving “the extension of healthy
               life expectancy of one billion people” and “the reducing of our environment impact by 50%”
               through initiatives of both resolving health and nutritional issues linked by food systems and
               promoting sustainability. Furthermore, in order to enhance the effectiveness of ASV Management,
               we select a “Company with Three Committees” that clearly separate supervision and execution by
               balancing “supervision of appropriate execution that reflects the opinions of stakeholders” and
               “business execution with a sense of speed.”
         3)    Views on the abilities and diversity of the Board of Directors as a whole
               The Company has the basic policy, considering the number of members, the percentage of Internal
               Directors and Independent Outside Directors, the percentage of persons who concurrently serve as
               Executive Officers, individual experience, abilities, insights, internationality, gender, race, ethnicity,
               nationality, country of origin or cultural background, etc., for the Board of Directors composed of
               Independent Outside Directors who can objectively supervise business execution from an
               independent standpoint, Internal Directors who concurrently serve as Executive Officers including
               the Chief Executive Officer, and Internal Directors who are members of the Audit Committee
               (Standing).
               In addition, in order to promote the separation of supervision and execution and further enhance the
               effectiveness of the management oversight function by the Board of Directors, the Independent
               Outside Directors shall occupy a majority, and the Chair of the Board of Directors shall be the
               Independent Outside Director.

*     The Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP) set out the beliefs and behaviors to which all Ajinomoto Group companies and each of
      those who work there are committed. The AGP serves as a written pledge to all of our stakeholders that Ajinomoto Group
      personnel will work earnestly to uphold these beliefs and behaviors.


             4)     Status of systems developed to ensure proper business operations
                    The Basic Policy on the Internal Control System, as resolved by the Board of Directors is as
                    follows:
                    1. System to Ensure that the Execution of Duties by Executive Officers and Employees of the Company Complies
                       with Laws and Regulations as well as the Articles of Incorporation

                      (1) By appointing an Independent Outside Director who can objectively supervise the execution of the
                           Company’s business from an independent standpoint, consisting a majority of the Board of Directors as
                           Independent Outside Directors, and appointing the Chairperson of the Board of Directors as an Independent
                           Outside Director, the Board of Directors shall strengthen the supervisory function for the execution of duties
                           by Executive Officers and employees of the Board of Directors, and ensure the appropriateness of business
                           execution.

                      (2) Establish the Nomination Committee and the Compensation Committee, both with a majority of members
                          comprising Independent Outside Directors, as voluntary committees of the Board of Directors in order to
                           enhance the transparency and objectivity of decisions related to the nomination of Directors, and the
                           compensation of Directors and corporate Executive Officers.

                      (3) The Audit Committee composed of Independent Outside Directors and Internal Directors who supervise
                          business execution based on a deep understanding of the Company’s business, with a majority of the
                           chairperson and committee members as Independent Outside Directors, and auditing the legality and
                           appropriateness of Company’s business execution by Executive Officers, plays an important role in the
                           function of “supervision of business execution,” and auditing the execution of the duties by Directors. The
                           Audit Committee inspects the minutes of the Nomination Committee and the Compensation Committee.

                      (4) The Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP) are established to illustrate the beliefs and behaviors which the
                           companies in the Ajinomoto Group and each individual who works there should uphold, and to provide a
                           written commitment to all of our stakeholders that they will uphold them.

                      (5) Establish the Group Compliance Committee (“GCC”) as a subordinate body of the Executive Committee for
                           the purpose of preventing any loss of corporate value resulting from misconduct and contributing to
                           strengthening of the management foundation and sustainable enhancement of the corporate value of the
                           Ajinomoto Group, and the GCC shall be primarily responsible for developing the global compliance
                           framework and strategies of the Ajinomoto Group, providing overall management of AGP, operating the
                           “Ajinomoto Group Hotline,” and responding to serious compliance incidents.




                                                                  - 104 -
  (6) The Company maintain a system for internal reporting in order to prevent misconduct before it happens and
      facilitate early detection and correction, and establishes the “Ajinomoto Group Hotline” as an internal
      reporting desk. The General Manager of the Legal & Compliance Dept. instructs relevant parties to
      investigate the facts of internal reports and consultations that are received, formulates countermeasures such
      as corrective steps, carries out these measures after deliberation with the GCC as necessary, and reports the
      results to the GCC.

  (7) The Internal Auditing Dept. conducts audit on business of operational organizations and Ajinomoto Group
      companies, reports the audit results to the Representative Executive Officer & President and the Audit
      Committee (Double Report), instructs organizations audited to correct matters pointed out in the audit, and
      checks on the implementation status of such corrections. Provided, however, that in order to ensure the
      independence of audits and maintain an effective and efficient auditing system, the latter shall be given
      priority in the event that the directions of the Representative Executive Officer & President conflict with the
      directions of the Audit Committee, in the directions of audit function.

      In order to ensure the reliability of financial reporting, the Internal Auditing Dept. assesses the internal
      control over financial reporting, reports the assessment results to the Representative Executive Officer &
      President and the Audit Committee, notifies organizations assessed of the assessment results, and instructs
      them to correct inadequacies, if any. Provided, however, that the latter shall be given priority in the event
      that the directions of the Representative Executive Officer & President conflict with the directions of the
      Audit Committee, in the directions of audit function.
      The Internal Auditing Dept. conducts investigations and audits at the direction of the Audit Committee.

2. System Concerning the Storage and Management of Information Related to the Execution of Duties by
   Executive Officers of the Company

       Store and manage documents and electronic records that record information related to the execution of
       duties by Executive Officers and Directors, including minutes of Board of Directors meetings, minutes of
       Executive Committee meetings, documents on decision-making, and minutes of various meetings in
       accordance with laws and regulations, and company regulations.

3. Regulations and Other Systems Concerning Management of Risk of Losses of the Company

  (1) The Risk Management Committee works with the Sustainability Committee to select and identify risks and
      opportunities based on Materiality as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto Group, making proposals
      to the Executive Committee. Additionally, the Committee formulates various measures for risk management,
      particularly for risks that management should take the initiative to address (such as geographical risks and
      information security risks), and formulates risk management measures and manages their progress in order
      to realize a strong corporate structure capable of responding promptly and appropriately to risks and crises.

  (2) The Sustainability Committee works with the Risk Management Committee to select and identify risks and
      opportunities based on Materiality, as well as assess their impact on the Ajinomoto Group, making proposals
      to the Executive Committee. The Committee then formulates countermeasures against risks and
      opportunities relevant to sustainability and manages their progress. In addition, the Sustainability Committee
      formulates the entire Ajinomoto Group’s sustainability strategy, promotes action themes (nutrition,
      environment, and society) based on this strategy, makes proposals and provides support for business plans
      from a sustainability viewpoint, and compiles internal information on ESG.

  (3) In the event of a crisis, establish task forces, etc., at relevant organizations, give the highest priority to
      human life, and strive to minimize losses to the Ajinomoto Group.

4. System to Ensure that the Execution of Duties by Executive Officers of the Company Is Performed Efficiently




                                                - 105 -
 (1) The Board of Directors meets once a month, in principle, to discuss and make decisions on important
      matters set forth in laws and regulations and the Articles of Incorporation as well as “Board of Directors
      Regulations,” etc., and supervises the execution of duties by Directors and Executive Officers.

 (2) The Executive Committee, which comprises the Representative Executive Officer and other Executive
     Officers nominated by the Representative Executive Officer, meets three times a month, in principle, to
      discuss and make decisions on important matters concerning the Company and the Ajinomoto Group set
      forth in “Global Governance Regulations.”

 (3) Clarify the scope of decision-making by the Board of Directors, the Executive Committee, Executive
     Officers and specified Ajinomoto Group companies, and proceed with the delegation of authority through
      the development, operation and review of company regulations.

 (4) Documents and other materials are submitted in electronic files to the Board of Directors and the Executive
      Committee in order to ensure the efficient operation of the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee.

5. System to Ensure the Appropriate Operation of Ajinomoto Group Companies

 (1) System related to reports to the Company related to the execution of duties by Directors of Ajinomoto Group
      companies

      Operating organizations are responsible for supervision of Ajinomoto Group companies they are in charge
      of in accordance with “Global Governance Regulations,” request reports related to the execution of duties
      by Directors of Ajinomoto Group companies, and refer important matters to decision-making by Executive
      Officers, the Executive Committee or the Board of Directors of the Company.

 (2) Regulations and other systems concerning management of risk of losses of Ajinomoto Group companies

      i. Make Ajinomoto Group companies enforce company regulations with the same effects as Ajinomoto
         Group common regulations depending on their respective business operations and management
         environments, etc.

      ii. In the event of a crisis at an Ajinomoto Group company, set up a task force, etc., as necessary and
         provide support in order to minimize losses to the Ajinomoto Group.

 (3) System to ensure that the execution of duties by Directors of Ajinomoto Group companies is performed
      efficiently

      i. Clarify the basic policy related to the supervision of Ajinomoto Group companies, make Ajinomoto
         Group companies enforce company regulations with the same effects as Ajinomoto Group common
         regulations, and provide guidance and support to ensure that the company regulations are operated
         effectively.

      ii. Conduct the appropriate delegation of authority to specified Ajinomoto Group companies in accordance
         with “Global Governance Regulations.”

  (4) System to ensure that the execution of duties by officers and employees of Ajinomoto Group companies
      complies with laws and regulations as well as the Articles of Incorporation

      i. Make Ajinomoto Group companies implement the AGP and have their officers and employees, etc.
         thoroughly comply with laws and regulations as well as the AGP.

      ii. Thoroughly make it widely known that officers and employees, etc. of Ajinomoto Group companies can
         make use of the desks to accept whistle-blowing set up in and outside the Company.

      iii. The Internal Auditing Dept. of the Company conducts audit on management and operations of Ajinomoto
         Group companies as well as assessment of the internal control over financial reporting.

      iv. At important Ajinomoto Group companies, even when they do not fall under the category of “Large
         Company” as defined by the Companies Act, assign Audit & Supervisory Board members (standing) in
         order to enhance the audit function.



                                             - 106 -
6. System to Ensure that the Audit by Audit Committee of the Company Is Conducted Effectively

  (1) Matters concerning employees, etc. who assist in the execution of duties by Audit Committee

      i. The Audit Committee is independently involved in the selection, dismissal and evaluation of the General
          Manager of the Internal Auditing Dept. to assist in their duties.

      ii. Within the Internal Auditing Dept., the Audit Committee staff necessary to assist the Audit Committee in
          its duties. The Audit Committee shall proactively engage in personnel evaluations, personnel changes,
          and disciplinary actions of the Audit Committee staff to enhance their independence from Executive
          Officers and ensure the effectiveness of the Audit Committee’s instructions to the Audit Committee staff.

  (2) System concerning reports to Audit Committee

      i. Executive Officers, when it detects facts that may cause significant losses to the Company or Ajinomoto
          Group companies, immediately reports them to the Member of the Audit Committee.

      ii. Employees of the Company as well as Directors, Audit & Supervisory Board members, and employees of
          Ajinomoto Group companies comply with requests for regular and non-regular reports from the Member
          of the Audit Committee or the Audit Committee of the Company. When they detect facts that may cause
          significant losses to the Company or Ajinomoto Group companies and they consider them as requiring
          urgent attention, they may report such facts directly to the Member of the Audit Committee or the Audit
          Committee of the Company.

      iii. Establish the “Hotline to Audit Committee” as the dedicated desk to report suspicions about the direct
          involvement in wrongdoing by officers of Ajinomoto Group companies.

      iv. No disadvantageous treatment is guaranteed for those who made reports in i. and ii. or whistleblowing
          for iii. for making such reports or whistle-blowing. This policy is thoroughly enforced at Ajinomoto
          Group companies.

  (3) Policy related to the handling of audit expenses

      i. The Company bears expenses required by the execution of duties of Audit Committee (including
          expenses related to the necessary solicitation of opinions from lawyers and other outside experts).

      ii. Regarding the audit-related expenses in i., make it a rule to set an annual budget and pay for expenses
          that arises in the year from the budget. However, expenses urgently or additionally required in relation to
          audit are also borne outside the predetermined annual budget.

  (4) Other systems to ensure that the audit by Audit Committee is conducted effectively

      i. Executive Officers make arrangements to allow Members of Audit Committee to attend important
         meetings held at operating organizations and offer other cooperation necessary for the execution of duties
          by Audit Committee, including submission of minutes of such meetings.

      ii. The Representative Executive Officer & President, other Executive Officers, and Member of Audit
          Committee or Audit Committee exchange information, regularly or on a non-regular basis, on
          compliance, risk management efforts and other management issues at the Company and Ajinomoto
          Group companies, and ensure better communication between Executive Officers, and Audit Committee.

7. System for the elimination of antisocial forces

  The Company clearly states to the AGP that we strictly avoid any involvement with organized antisocial forces,
  which pose a threat to civic order and safety, stand resolutely against organized antisocial forces and refuse any
   and all inappropriate demands, and the GCC seeks to make the AGP well known across the Ajinomoto Group in
   cooperation with relevant divisions, including providing support and coordinating activities to make the AGP
   prevail throughout the Ajinomoto Group companies.




                                              - 107 -
5)   Overview of management status of systems to ensure proper business operations
     Based on the Basic Policy on the Internal Control System, the Company has developed and
     properly operated an internal control system. The main initiatives conducted during the fiscal year
     ended March 31, 2026 were as indicated below.

     1. Compliance initiatives

       (1) The Business Conduct Committee makes continuous efforts to ensure thorough compliance with the
           Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP). During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, as well, the AGP Worksite
           Meeting were held at workplaces nationwide (33 sessions were held within the Company) under the theme
           of “creating a workplace culture that respects each individual’s uniqueness and values.” These study
           sessions provided opportunities to promote greater understanding of AGP and to inspect compliance risks in
           workplaces, and we identified compliance issues in workplaces and elicited opinions on Company-wide
           initiatives. In addition, the AGP basic principles were revised to respond to societal expectations arising
           from changes in the external environment and to more clearly articulate the Ajinomoto Group’s commitment
           to compliance. Furthermore, to increase awareness and encourage use of the “Ajinomoto Group Hotline,”
           the Company instructed Group companies to display hotline posters and distributed explanatory videos
           throughout the Group. These activities were reported from the Business Conduct Committee to the
           Executive Committee and the Board of Directors.

           Effective April 1, 2026, the Business Conduct Committee was reorganized on a global basis and the Group
           Compliance Committee (“GCC”) was established. The GCC is primarily responsible for developing the
           global compliance framework and strategies of the Ajinomoto Group. The GCC’s deliberations and activities
           are reported to the Executive Committee and the Board of Directors.

       (2) During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Internal Auditing Dept. audited operations for the
           Company’s business operation organizations and Group companies (at a total of 30 sites).

     2. Risk management initiatives

       (1) The Risk Management Committee met four times to select and identify risks and opportunities based on
           important issues (Materiality). It identified cyberattacks by outside parties, a global trade war, the escalation
           of the Taiwan Strait issue, and major earthquake or flooding damage in the Tokyo metropolitan area as risks
           that management should take the initiative in addressing, and implemented countermeasures accordingly.
           These activities were reported from the Risk Management Committee to the Executive Committee and the
           Board of Directors.

       (2) The Sustainability Committee met three times to select and identify risks and opportunities based on
           important issues (Materiality), formulate countermeasures, and review related targets and KPIs. Promotion
           and monitoring of these initiatives were carried out in collaboration with personnel in business divisions,
           regional divisions, and corporate departments.

       (3) The Investment, Loan, and Business Scrutiny Committee met 12 times. The M&A Committee met nine
           times to deliberate M&As. The Quality Assurance Committee and the Occupational Safety and Health
           Committee each met two times, reviewed the Group’s overall activities, and confirmed its initiatives for
           addressing critical issues.

     3. Global governance initiatives

       (1) The Board of Directors met 19 times. The Board of Directors continued its efforts to improve the efficiency
           of Board operations and set up an annual agenda plan based on the “New Seven Important Management
           Matters” that have a significant impact on corporate value over the medium to long term, which are matters
           that should be discussed by the Board of Directors, in order to achieve our Vision set forth in the Medium -
           Term ASV Management 2030 Roadmap.




                                                   - 108 -
           (2) The Executive Committee met 33 times. The Committee reported on and discussed important matters related
               to the Company and Group companies, and determined matters related to business execution appropriately,
               as stipulated in the Global Governance Regulations.

           (3) The Global Governance Regulations were systematically revised to clarify delegation of authority and
               accountability and to improve the efficiency and sophistication of operational activities at work sites. As a
               result, the Group further enhanced the effectiveness of its global governance while maintaining Group-wide
               control.

         4. Initiatives related to auditing by the Audit Committee

           (1) As of March 31, 2026, nine personnel (seven full-time personnel and two personnel with concurrent
               positions) were assigned as staff to assist the Audit Committee in its duties. They have been given access
               privileges to essential Company information, perform comprehensive monitoring when appropriate, and
               coordinate with the Internal Auditing Dept. to ensure the effectiveness of auditing by the Audit Committee.
               The Audit Committee met 16 times during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.

           (2) The General Manager of the Internal Auditing Dept. reported the results of the internal audit to the Audit
               Committee meeting and reported on internal audit activities and evaluations of internal control related to
               financial reporting to the Audit Committee once every three months. They also responded to reporting
               requests and conducted hearings as necessary. When matters with the potential to cause significant losses for
               the Company or Group companies are discovered, they are reported in turn to Members of the Audit
               Committee, but no such matters were discovered during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026.


6)       Summary of Limited Liability Agreements
     The Company has entered into an agreement with Independent Outside Directors to limit their
     liability for damages under Article 427, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act. Financial limitations on
     liability for damage based on this Agreement shall be the aggregate amount as stipulated in the
     respective items of Article 425, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act.

7)       Summary of limited liability agreements for officers, etc.
      The Company has concluded a liability insurance policy for officers, etc., with an insurance
     company, as stipulated in Article 430-3, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act. If a claim for damages is
     filed by a shareholder or a third party, those damages such as damages and dispute costs that the
     insured is to bear will be covered by the insurance policy. The persons insured by the liability policy
     are the Directors and Executive Officers of the Company, and the Directors, Audit & Supervisory
     Board Members and Corporate Officers of the Company’s subsidiaries. The Company will bear all
     premium payments for the insurance policy. The insurance policy will be renewed on expiration of
     the term of contract.

8)       Provisions in the Articles of Incorporation concerning Directors
     -      Number of Directors
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that the Company shall have 12 Directors or less.
     -      Requirements for resolutions on the election of Directors
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that resolutions on the election of Directors shall be
            decided by shareholders who have one third or more of the voting rights of shareholders entitled
            to exercise their voting rights being in attendance at the Ordinary General Meeting of
            Shareholders and when a majority of the votes of such shareholders in attendance are in
            agreement. The Articles of Incorporation also stipulate that resolutions on the election of
            Directors shall not be conducted by cumulative voting.




                                                      - 109 -
9)       Matters for resolution by the General Meeting of Shareholders that can be resolved on by the Board
         of Directors
     -      Purchase of treasury stock
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that pursuant to Article 165, Paragraph 2 of the
            Companies Act, the Company may acquire its own shares through market transactions, etc. by
            resolution of the Board of Directors. This provision enables the Company to flexibly repurchase
            treasury stock to improve shareholder returns and capital efficiency, and to replenish any
            shortfall of treasury stock under the additional purchase program for shares less than one unit.
     -      Distribution of surplus, etc.
            The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that, in order to flexibly return profits to shareholders and
            implement capital policy, the Company may, by resolution of the Board of Directors, determine
            matters stipulated in respective items of Article 459, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act,
            including the distribution of surplus. They also stipulate that dividends of surplus may be paid to
            shareholders or registered share pledgees recorded in the final shareholders’ register as of March
            31 or September 30 each year. Except in cases where infectious diseases or natural disasters may
            affect the holding and operation of the General Meeting of Shareholders, it is the Company’s
            policy that year-end dividends of surplus shall, in principle, be subject to resolution at the
            General Meeting of Shareholders.

10) Requirements for special resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders
         The Articles of Incorporation stipulate that special resolutions of the General Meeting of
         Shareholders, as provided in Article 309, Paragraph 2 of the Companies Act, require the attendance
         of shareholders holding one-third or more of the total voting rights exercisable, and the approval of
         two-thirds or more of the voting rights of the shareholders present. The purpose of this is to
         facilitate the operation of the Meeting of Shareholders by providing an easier quorum requirement
         for special resolutions at the General Meeting of Shareholders.

   3.   Details regarding the function and role of Independent Outside Directors in corporate
        governance and the criteria or policy regarding their independence
        The Company has a basic policy considering the number of members, the percentage of Internal
        Directors and Independent Outside Directors, the percentage of persons who concurrently serve
        as Executive Officers, individual experience, abilities, insights, internationality, gender, race,
        ethnicity, nationality, country of origin or cultural background, etc., for the Board of Directors
        composed of Independent Outside Directors who can objectively supervise business execution
        from an independent standpoint, Internal Directors who concurrently serve as Executive Officers
        including the Chief Executive Officer, and Internal Directors who are Members of the Audit
        Committee (Standing). In addition, in order to promote the separation of supervision and
        execution and further enhance the effectiveness of the management oversight function by the
        Board of Directors, the Independent Outside Directors shall occupy a majority, and the Chair of
        the Board of Directors shall be the Independent Outside Director.
        There are no special interests between the Independent Outside Directors and the Company, and
        the Company has determined that the Independent Outside Directors have the independence
        necessary to fulfill their functions and roles.
        Mr. George Nakayama had served as Representative Director and Chairperson of Daiichi Sankyo
        Co., Ltd. until June 2020 and served as full-time advisor of the same company from June of the
        same year to June 2025. In addition, Ajinomoto Co., Inc. had a business relationship in the past
        with Daiichi Sankyo Co., Ltd. However, there were no such interactions in the fiscal year ended
        March 31, 2026. Therefore, Mr. Nakayama fulfills the requirements of independence to serve as
        an Independent Outside Director of Ajinomoto Co., Inc.
        The Company’s Standards for Determining the Independence of Outside Directors are as
        follows:
        Outside Directors must not fall under any of the following categories to be considered independent.
        (1) Said person regards the Company as a key customer, or is an executive officer for such a party.
        (2) Said person is a key customer of the Company, or is an executive officer for such a party.
        (3) Said person is a consultant, accounting specialist or legal specialist who has received substantial monetary or
             other assets (other than director compensation) from the Company. (if the person receiving said assets is a
             corporate entity, association, or other such organization, this stipulation extends to members of that
             organization.)
        (4) Said person who falls under criteria (1), (2), or (3) above at any time within a one-year period before the
             proposed appointment.
        (5) Said person is a relative (a relative up through the second degree of kinship) of any person (other than those
            deemed unimportant) falling under criteria 1), 2), or 3) below.
            1) A person falling under criteria (1), (2), (3), or (4) above.
            2) A person who is an executive officer of a subsidiary of the Company.
            3) A person who falls under criteria 2) above or is an executive officer of the Company, at any time within a
                one-year period before the proposed appointment.




                                                   - 128 -
       Notes:
       1. A person who “regards the Company as a key customer,” refers to a person who, within the most recent
          business year, received from the Company an amount corresponding to 2% of that party’s annual consolidated
          sales or ¥100 million, whichever is higher.
       2. A person who is “a key customer of the Company,” refers to a person who, within the most recent business
          year, paid to the Company an amount corresponding to 2% of our annual consolidated sales or ¥100 million,
          whichever is higher.
       3. A person who “has received substantial monetary or other assets from the Company,” refers to a person who,
           within the most recent business year, has received from the Company monies/property in an amount
           corresponding to 2% of that party’s sales/ total revenues or ¥10 million, whichever is higher.

3. Main activities of Audit Committee members
    The Audit Committee operates under the basic policy of “preventing misconduct and
    contributing to high-quality corporate governance and the enhancement of corporate value by
    promoting lawful and socially responsible business execution throughout the Group through
    audits of the execution of duties by Directors and Executive Officers as representatives of
    stakeholders.” During the current fiscal year, the Audit Committee focused primarily on the
    following key areas: ensuring execution abilities related to the 2030 Roadmap and reviewing
    progress against the Roadmap; building management foundations, including Group-wide
    governance frameworks; reviewing progress in IT governance initiatives; responding to
    geopolitical risks related to raw material procurement, logistics, and other factors; and
    addressing sustainability-related disclosures, including efforts toward human rights risks.
 1) Monitoring the status of governance
    Audit Committee members attended meetings of the Board of Directors, auditing the
    proceedings and resolutions, and expressing their opinions when necessary. Full-time Audit
    Committee members participated in key internal meetings and committees, such as the
    Executive Committee and the Business Conduct Committee (reorganized as the Group
    Compliance Committee from April 2026). Some Independent Outside Directors serving as
    Audit Committee members also serve concurrently as members of the Nomination Committee
    and the Compensation Committee.

                                            - 134 -
  All Audit Committee members held quarterly meetings, four times a year, with the
  Representative Executive Officer & President and the Executive Officer & Senior Vice
  President in charge of corporate affairs. Full-time Audit Committee members also held
  individual meetings with Executive Officers to exchange views on issues in their respective
  areas of responsibility. Where necessary, the Audit Committee provided recommendations to
  enhance the effectiveness of corporate governance based on these dialogues. The Audit
  Committee also received reports from and engaged in opinion exchanges with Directors,
  Executive Officers, and department heads as necessary.
  The Audit Committee monitored the operation of the governance framework, including the
  delegation of management execution to Executive Officers and the exercise of appropriate
  supervisory functions by the Board of Directors, in accordance with the Regulations of the
  Board of Directors and the Group Shared Policy on Governance (GGP), and reported and
  provided its opinions to the Board of Directors. The status of GGP-related decision-making
  operations was continuously monitored, shared and confirmed by the Audit Committee, and
  status updates and recommendations were provided during quarterly meetings with the
  Representative Executive Officer & President and the Executive Officer & Senior Vice
  President in charge of corporate affairs. In March 2026, the Audit Committee received a report
  from management on the results of the effectiveness verification conducted regarding the
  operation of the internal control system during FY2025 and offered recommendations aimed at
  continuous improvement.
2) Addressing risks
  For risks related to safety, quality, environment, information management (including personal
  information), and labor management, full-time Audit Committee members attended the
  Business Conduct Committee (reorganized as the Group Compliance Committee from April
  2026), the Sustainability Committee, and the Risk Management Committee to monitor
  compliance and risk management initiatives.
  The Audit Committee also continued monitoring the implementation of the whistleblowing
  system. Through the Audit Committee Hotline, which plays a key role in the system, Audit
  Committee members directly responded to reports concerning officers, including those of
  group companies. The status of these responses is deliberated and reported by the Audit
  Committee and subsequently reported to the Board of Directors.
3) Audits and investigations
  While making full use of internal audits conducted by the internal auditing department, Audit
  Committee members also engaged directly in audit activities to enhance the effectiveness of
  management audits through a “hybrid audit” approach. In the current fiscal year, audits and
  investigations were conducted at 16 domestic and overseas group company sites, in
  combination with departmental audits. Recommendations and proposals were made from the
  perspectives of management, human resources, finance, governance, and internal control. The
  results of these audits and investigations were shared at the Audit Committee Communication
  Meetings and subsequently reported to the Board of Directors.

(ii) Status of internal audits
   1. Purpose of internal audits
        The purpose of internal audits at the Company is to contribute to the achievement of
        management objectives, the strengthening of corporate governance, and the enhancement of
        public trust. This is accomplished by the internal auditing department independently evaluating
        the adequacy and effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal control processes
        within the Company and its group organizations, and promoting improvements.

   2. Organization, personnel and procedures
        The internal auditing department conducts operational audits of business operation
        organizations and both management and operational audits of consolidated subsidiaries, in
        accordance with the Internal Audit Regulations and related internal rules. In principle, internal
        audits cover all business operating units and all consolidated subsidiaries. From among these
        organizations, each year, the General Manager of the Internal Auditing Department determines
        the audit targets using a risk-based approach that considers factors such as findings from
        previous audits and the time elapsed since the last audit. An audit plan is then formulated,
        identifying priority items to be verified for each audit target. This plan is reported in advance to
        the Audit Committee, approved by the Executive Committee, and subsequently reported to the
        Board of Directors before audits are conducted.
        Following each audit, the General Manager submits an internal audit report (a double report) to
        both the Representative Executive Officer & President and the Audit Committee, and sends a
        copy to the Executive Officer responsible for the audited organization and its general manager.
        Audited organizations are required to address the identified issues, and the internal auditing
        department follows up on the status of corrective actions. If there is any inconsistency between
        instructions from the Representative Executive Officer & President and those from the Audit
        Committee regarding an audit, the instructions of the Audit Committee take precedence.
        In addition to submitting the internal audit report, the department provides monthly updates
        and exchanges opinions with the Audit Committee and the Representative Executive Officer &
        President. A report is also submitted to the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee
        semiannually.
        As of March 31, 2026, 27 personnel are involved in internal audits. These personnel bring
        diverse experience in areas such as domestic and international business, production, research,
        sales, finance and accounting, legal affairs, human resources, intellectual property, and IT. To
        enable them to contribute effectively to achieving management goals as audit professionals, the
        internal auditing department has defined a target auditor profile using a skill map and is
        working to continuously enhance their competencies through a structured training program
        based on that map. As part of these efforts, the Company encourages and supports employees
        in obtaining the Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) certification (as of the end of March 2026,
        nine employees hold this qualification).
        The internal auditing department works closely with the internal auditing departments of both
        domestic and overseas consolidated subsidiaries to enhance audit quality across the Group.
        When the internal auditing departments of consolidated subsidiaries are assessed to have
        adequate systems and activities, the internal auditing department may rely on their audit results
        and omit all or part of its own procedures. Currently, the internal auditing department relies on
        audits of certain target organizations performed by the internal auditing departments of five
        domestic and four overseas subsidiaries (the “reliance parties”). Organizations audited by these

                                            - 137 -
    reliance parties are not included in the internal auditing department’s audit plan; instead, each
    reliance party establishes its own audit plan in consultation with the Company’s internal
    auditing department. The General Manager of the Internal Auditing Department also reports
    the results of audits conducted by the reliance parties to the Representative Executive Officer
    & President and the Audit Committee members. As of March 31, 2026, 18 personnel are
    involved in internal audits at domestic reliance parties and 26 at overseas reliance parties.
    Every year, the internal auditing department conducts self-assessments, and for reliance parties,
    the department performs evaluations based on their respective self-assessments. In March
    2026, the Company also conducted its external evaluation once every five years, which helps
    ensure audit effectiveness and improve audit quality.
    The Company’s internal auditing department also conducts evaluations and reports on internal
    control over financial reporting in accordance with the Financial Instruments and Exchange
    Act.

    General Manager of the Internal Auditing Department reports quarterly to the Audit

    department, and exchanges opinions with each other.

    5. Audit firm selection policy, reasons, and evaluation
            In accordance with the procedures for appointing Accounting Auditors set forth in the
            Company’s Audit Committee Audit Standards, and based on the “Standards for the
            Appointment and Reappointment of Accounting Auditors” established by the Audit
            Committee, the Committee conducted evaluations of the Accounting Auditor and interviews
            with relevant parties. It confirms the appropriateness of the Accounting Auditor’s
            performance, audit framework, independence, and professional capabilities.
            In the event that the Accounting Auditor is recognized to have fallen under any of the items in
            Article 340, Paragraph 1 of the Companies Act, the Audit Committee shall dismiss the
            Accounting Auditor, based on the consent of all members of the Audit Committee. In this
            case, a member of the Audit Committee selected by the Audit Committee shall report the fact
            that the Accounting Auditor was dismissed and the reasons for the dismissal at the first
            General Meeting of Shareholders convened after the dismissal.
            In addition, if the Audit Committee recognizes that it is necessary to change the Accounting
            Auditor, such as cases when it conducts a comprehensive evaluation in accordance with
            evaluation indicators related to the Accounting Auditor’s qualifications, independence from
            the Company, expertise, and other criteria, and finds that there are issues preventing the
            Accounting Auditor from executing its duties, then it shall determine the content of a proposal
            related to the dismissal or non-reappointment of the Accounting Auditor to be submitted at the
            General Meeting of Shareholders.
            In accordance with the aforementioned policy, the Audit Committee conducted an evaluation
            of the audit firm’s performance and capabilities. For more information, please refer to the “(i)
            Status of audits by Audit Committee, 3. Main activities of Audit Committee members, 6)
            Evaluation of the Accounting Auditor and decisions on reappointment or non-reappointment.”

(4) Compensations for officers
Compensation for the fiscal year under review
     (i)    Matters regarding policies on determining the amount of compensations of officers and
            calculation method thereof
           1. Basic principles for officers’ compensations decisions
            Matters regarding policies on determining the amount of compensations of officers and
            calculation method thereof are decided by the Compensation Committee. The basic policy on
            determining officer compensation is as follows:

            1) In line with the Ajinomoto Group Policies (AGP), it will lead to medium- to long-term
               expansion of the corporate value

            2) The level of compensations is sufficiently competitive with the market level

            3) Compensations will be determined through a transparent process that is accountable to
               stakeholders

           2. Outline of compensations for officers

            1) Compensations of Executive Officers (including persons who concurrently serve as Directors)
                Comprised of the Basic Compensation, the Short-term Incentives (hereinafter referred to as
                “STI”), and the Medium-term Stock-based Incentives (hereinafter referred to as “MTI”), the
                details of which are as follow:
                i) Basic compensation
                The Basic Compensation is a monetary compensation that is paid every month to fully
                demonstrate the qualities and abilities that drive corporate growth and to meet the
                responsibilities of employees. A fixed amount is paid monthly.
                ii) Short-term Incentives (STI)
                The STI is a monetary compensation that is paid at the end of June once a year, depending on
                the performance evaluation of the entire Company and each individual after the end of the
                fiscal year, as an incentive to encourage steady achievement of performance targets for a
                single fiscal year and appropriate management.
                iii) Medium-term Stock-based Incentives (MTI)
                The MTI is a performance-linked compensation that is assessed using a predetermined
                evaluation indicator after the end of the three fiscal years commencing on April 1, 2023
                (hereinafter referred to as the “3-Year Period”) with the aim of achieving sustained medium-
                to long-term improvement in business performance and increasing corporate value of the
                Ajinomoto Group, and is paid in the Company’s shares and the amount equivalent to the
                conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares. The maximum amount of monies the
                Company contributes to the stock-granting trust (hereinafter referred to as the “Trust”) for the
                MTI is ¥2.2 billion for the 3-Year Period covered and the maximum amount of the
                Company’s shares to be acquired by the Trust in the money provided to the Trust is 1.1
                million. The number of the Company’s shares, etc. to be used for payment of MTI is obtained
                as follows. Performance evaluation index for each performance evaluation indicator
                (calculated from the target achievement rate and assessment weighting) is multiplied by the
                predetermined standard amount for each job position. Then, the total amount obtained
                (hereinafter referred to as the “amount of MTI”) is divided by the closing price (¥2,303.0) of
                the Company’s shares on March 31, 2023, to yield the number of shares to be used for
                payment of MTI. Half of the MTI will be delivered in the form of Company’s shares, and the
                remaining half will be delivered in cash to be used for payment of income tax, etc., therefore
                the Trust will convert this half to cash by selling the shares on the market and then paying the
                amount equivalent to the conversion and disposal of the Company’s shares. For Executive
                Officers who are non-Japan residents or Foreign Directors and Officers (as defined in 3. 2) ii)
                below), the MTI will be delivered in cash, using the currency specified in the “Standard
                amount by position.” However, Executive Officers and their successors who have been
                resolved by the Compensation Committee of the Company that they are not appropriate to

                                                  - 142 -
     receive the MTI in light of the purpose of such compensation system may not receive such
     compensation, and in the event a resolution is made by the Compensation Committee of the
     Company that it is not appropriate to pay the MTI to Executive Officers in light of the
     purpose of such compensation system, the Company may seek the return of such
     compensation from the person who received such compensation.
     The Company uses ROIC (return on invested capital after tax) and relative TSR (versus
     TOPIX) as economic value indicators, greenhouse gas emissions reduction rate and number
     of individuals whose healthy life expectancy has extended as social value indicators, and
     employee engagement score, percentage of global female managers, and corporate brand
     value as intangible asset enhancement indicators.

 2) Compensations for Independent Outside Directors and Internal Directors who are members of
    the Audit Committee
     The compensations for Independent Outside Directors shall be based solely on the Basic
     Compensation, which shall be paid monthly in a fixed amount of cash. The compensations for
     the Internal Directors who are members of the Audit Committee shall be based solely on the
     Basic Compensation, which shall be paid monthly in a fixed amount of cash.


3. Policy on determining the amount of compensation for individual officers

 1) How to determine compensations
     The amount of compensation will be determined by job position based on the responsibilities
     of supervision and execution performed by officers.

 2) How to determine levels of compensations
     i) Compensation levels for Internal Directors and Executive Officers are based on the 75th
     percentile (the top 25%) of that level (based on the results of surveys conducted by external
     organizations covering a substantial number of comparable companies, including companies
     in other industries).
     When such Internal Directors or Executive Officers concurrently serve as a president of an
     overseas group company of the Company, the Company will pay allowances due to overseas
     assignments and adjust the amount of compensations in consideration of the amount
     equivalent to individual income taxes that would be levied if the Internal Director or
     Executive Officer worked in Japan (reference: performance-linked compensation is calculated
     based on the income tax equivalent amount in accordance with the “Table of Withholding
     Tax Rates on Bonuses” issued by the National Tax Agency), and the amount of compensation
     from the overseas group company of the Company. If individual income taxes are incurred in
     the host country, the overseas group companies will bear the amount equivalent to such taxes.
     ii) Notwithstanding of the above, compensation levels for Internal Directors and Executive
     Officers who have the closest relationship with countries (or regions) other than Japan
     (“Foreign Directors and Officers”) are based on 50th to 75th percentiles (top 25% to 50%) of
     the level based on the results of surveys conducted by external organizations on companies
     that are similar in size and business type in the countries (or regions).
     The Company will adjust the amount of compensations from the Company in consideration of
     the amount of taxes that would be levied if they worked in that most closely related country
     or region. In addition to the above, if individual income taxes are incurred in Japan due to the
     appointment of a seconded person from an overseas group company to the Company as an
     Internal Director or Executive Officer, the Company will bear the amount equivalent to such
     taxes.
     iii) The level of compensations for Independent Outside Directors is based on the 75th
     percentile (the top 25%) of that level (based on the results of surveys conducted by external
     organizations on us and about 20 companies with a Nominating Committee, etc. that are
     similar in size to the Company).

       the number of months served in a specific executive role, countered from the month
       following the month of appointment (or from the month of appointment if the
       appointment date is the first day of the month) and continues through the month in
       which the officer retires from the position.
       If the start and end months are the same, the month count shall be one. However, the
       total number of months in position shall not exceed the total months served as an
       Executive Officer.
(vi)      Reference: Description of performance-linked compensation under Article 34,

(v)       Performance index formula
         A performance evaluation index is calculated for each performance indicator based on
         the formulas presented in Table 1 and Table 2 below. However, for the performance
         evaluation indicators classified as “Social value indicators” and “Intangible asset
         enhancement indicators,” the achievement rate shall be 1.0 if the target is achieved and 0
         if the target is not achieved. The maximum achievement rate of the performance
         evaluation indicator for the “Economic value indicator” is capped at 1.4. If the
         achievement rate falls below the non-payment standards defined in Table 2, the rate shall
         be deemed to be 0.6, regardless of the non-payment standards specified therein and the
         performance evaluation index for each performance evaluation indicator is then
         calculated accordingly.
         Notwithstanding the foregoing, the performance evaluation of an Executive Officer who
         falls under ii) (b) b) or (c) b) of “(i) The amount of Medium-term Stock-based Incentives
         (MTI)” shall be deemed to have achieved 100% of the target for each performance
         evaluation indicator. However, this exception shall not apply if the relevant event occurs
         between February 1 of the final fiscal year and the last day of the target period.

   Notes:
   1. ROIC (Return on Invested Capital after tax) is calculated based on the following formula. All figures are
      consolidated amounts.
      ROIC (Return on Invested Capital after tax) = (Operating profit after tax for the fiscal year) ÷ ((Invested
      capital for the fiscal year + Invested capital for the previous fiscal year) ÷ 2)
      Operating profit after tax = Operating profit x (1 - Income taxes ÷ Profit before income taxes)
      Invested capital = (Equity attributable to owners of the parent company) + (Interest-bearing debt)
      Interest-bearing debt = (Short-term borrowings) + (Commercial papers) + (Current portion of bonds) +
      (Current portion of long-term borrowings) + (Corporate bonds) + (Long-term borrowings) + (Short-term
      lease liabilities) + (Long-term lease liabilities)
   2. Relative TSR is calculated based on the following formula.
      Relative TSR = (Total Company shareholder return at the end of the latest fiscal year) ÷ (Total TOPIX
      shareholder return including dividends for the corresponding period used to calculate total Company
      shareholder return)
      Total Company shareholder return at the end of the latest fiscal year = (Share price at the end of the latest
      fiscal year + Cumulative amount of dividends per share of four fiscal years prior to the latest fiscal year
      through the latest fiscal year) ÷ Share price at the end of the fiscal year five years prior to the latest fiscal
      year
      Total TOPIX shareholder return including dividends for corresponding period used to calculate total
      Company shareholder return = TOPIX total returns including dividends at the end of the latest fiscal year
      ÷ TOPIX total returns including dividends at the end of the fiscal year five years prior to the latest fiscal
      year

      achievement process” and determined by achieved or not achieved.
   4. The Corporate brand value is evaluated by using the “Best Japan Brands” published by Interbrand.
   5. ROIC (Return on Invested Capital after tax) achievement rate is calculated by the weighted total value of
      each fiscal year.
